rumours: Wayrest and Daggerfall are bowing to each other again this season. When two Breton kings bow that low, somebody's about to get stabbed under the table.
The Orcs have rebuilt Orsinium, bigger than before. The Breton lords keep talking about doing something about it. The Breton smiths keep quietly buying Orcish steel.
A hedge-witch in Stormhaven will read your fortune in a bowl of milk for two septims. For five she'll tell you whose fortune you're about to ruin.
Every Breton house has a mage in the family tree and a Daedra somewhere in the cellar. The trick is not to mention either at dinner.
Knights of the Dragon and Knights of the Rose both rode out to the Bangkorai pass this summer. Neither will say what for. Both came back with fewer horses.
Shornhelm's nobles are feuding again. One of them sent another a cake. Nobody's eaten it. It's been sitting on the council table for a week, and everybody's watching it.
legends: The Bretons say their grandmothers' grandmothers were Nedes who married the elves of the Direnni, and that this is why a Breton can always talk his way into a tower and out of a dungeon. The Direnni tower still stands on its island in the bay, and old families leave a candle burning toward it on the longest night of the year, so the elves will remember they are owed nothing.

When the knights of Daggerfall and the warriors of Sentinel laid siege to Orsinium for thirty years in the First Era, the Orcs inside held out by eating their leather, then their boots, then their pride. When the walls finally fell, the Breton knights found the last Orc defenders sitting on the gate with their axes across their knees, too weak to stand and too proud to lie down. The Orcs have told that story to their children ever since, and they tell it as a victory.

Somewhere under the Wrothgar snows lies the old Orsinium, the first one, and the Orc smiths say its forges have never gone cold. Stand on the right mountainside on a still winter night and you can hear hammers under the ice.

songs.title: The Courteous Knife
lines: ~O bow to the Duke and bow to the Duchess,
~and kiss the cold hand of the Count;
~smile as you pour, keep your back to the door,
~and never let on what you've found.
~For the knife in the court is a courteous knife,
~and it says 'by your leave' as it goes.

songs.title: Hammers Under the Snow
lines: ~They burned our city, so we built it higher,
~they burned it again, so we built it of fire;
~count up the burnings, count up the stones,
~Orsinium stands on a mountain of bones.

rumours: The Crowns and the Forebears are at each other's throats again. Same as every year. Only now there's no Empire to stop them and no Dominion to unite them, so it's real swords instead of polite ones.
Hammerfell threw the Thalmor out on its own, after the Emperor signed it away. Ask any Redguard about the White-Gold Concordat and watch his hand go to his sword.
The sword-singers are teaching again, in the old schools near Sentinel. They say an Ansei can make a blade out of nothing but his own spirit. I've seen it. It's not nothing.

Alik'r nomads came in from the deep desert talking about a city of sand that rose out of the dunes for one night, with lights in its windows. Nomads say a lot of things. They don't usually all say the same thing.
The Forebear merchants of Taneth are buying Dwemer brass by the cartload. Nobody knows why. The Crowns say they're building a fleet. The Forebears say they're decorating.
Orcs of Orsinium came down the Bangkorai pass to sell steel in Elinhir. Nobody fought anybody. My grandfather wouldn't believe it.
legends: When Yokuda sank into the sea, the Ra Gada sailed east in the ships of Frandar Hunding, carrying nothing but their swords and their ancestors' names. The first thing they did when they reached the shore of Hammerfell was cut down everything in their way. The second thing was to bury their dead properly. A Redguard will forgive you for the first. Never for neglecting the second.

The Hiradirge was the warrior's path of the old Yokudan sword-masters, and the greatest among them could cut the very air between two moments. The Ansei say Frandar Hunding wrote the whole of the sword's teaching in a single book, and that a true student reads it once, then closes it forever, because the rest must be learned from the blade.

The Alik'r nomads say that the desert is the bed of a sea that once loved a man so much it dried itself out to follow him inland. Wherever you find a well in the sand, they say, the sea is still weeping for him.

songs.title: The Crossing
lines: ~We left the drowned land singing,
~our fathers' bones aboard;
~we came ashore with nothing
~but the memory of the sword.
~And when they ask what Hammerfell is,
~we answer with the sword.

rumours: The Thalmor say Valenwood is a loyal province of the Dominion. The Bosmer say the trees haven't been asked. Nobody's brave enough to ask the trees.
Colovian loggers keep crossing the border to fell graht-oaks east of Elden Root. The wardens keep sending back their axes. The loggers don't always come with them.
The Silvenar's a good man, they say, and the Green Lady's a fierce one. Between them they speak for every Bosmer. That's a lot of talking to do, and the Thalmor are always listening.
Bosmer won't cut a living branch, but they'll eat a man they killed in battle within three days. Visitors tend to find the first rule charming and the second one less so.
There's talk of the Wild Hunt in Grahtwood again. My mother says it's only talk. My mother also nailed a deer skull over our door.
legends: Before the Green Pact the Bosmer were formless, and changed shape as the forest did. Y'ffre the Storyteller sang them into the shapes they wear now, and asked in return only that they never harm the green. Each Spinner keeps a strand of that first song, and when the last strand is forgotten, the Spinners say, the Bosmer will lose their shapes again.

The Wild Hunt is the oldest and worst rite of the Bosmer. When the elders call it, the hunters drink a draught and become beasts, a tide of teeth and claws with no master, that runs until it has devoured its target or itself. It has been called only a few times in history. The Bosmer do not say how many. Every time they are asked, they look away.

songs.title: The Hound's Promise
lines: ~Leave the tree and take the deer,
~leave the root and take the boar,
~the forest feeds the hound that's true,
~and the Huntsman keeps the score.

rumours: The Thalmor took Summerset over in the name of the old Aldmeri glory. Now the old Aldmeri glory needs a stamped permit to visit its cousins on Auridon.
Maormer sails off the southern capes again. The Sea Elves never stop trying, and the Altmer never stop pretending they're not worried.
The Crystal Tower's lights burned blue three nights running. The Sapiarchs say it means nothing. The Sapiarchs never say anything means nothing, so that means something.
The genealogists of the Directorate came to my neighbour's house with measuring rods. His family's been on the island for four thousand years. Apparently that's not quite long enough.
Fishermen out past the western shoals swear they saw Artaeum through the fog. Every year somebody does. Every year the Psijics don't send a letter.
Summerset's the most beautiful place in Tamriel, and the quietest. Nobody talks too loud here. The walls are white and very thin.
legends: The Altmer say that when the world was made, the gods who helped make it lost their divinity in the act, and that the Altmer are their mortal descendants. That is why the Altmer strive so hard to be perfect, and why they grieve so quietly: every one of them is mourning something they never had.

The Crystal Tower of Summerset, the Altmer say, was raised over the place where the first elves came ashore, and its light holds the memory of everything the elves have learned since. The Sapiarchs guard its upper chambers, and the deepest of them, it is said, holds a single shelf on which the Psijics once left a book. No Sapiarch has ever read it. No Sapiarch has ever dared to take it down.

During the Oblivion Crisis, when the gates opened across Summerset, the Altmer held the Daedra off without an Emperor, without the Legion, and without asking for help. The Thalmor tell this story as proof that the elves need no one. The old ones who were there tell it differently: they say they asked, and no one came.

songs.title: White Walls
lines: ~White walls, white towers, white gulls on the quay,
~my love had a crooked smile and they took her away.
~The genealogist came with his silver and his book,
~and the sea was so blue that I could not look.

rumours: The Knights of the Rose have the docks quiet at last. Quiet docks in Wayrest, imagine. The fishwives don't know what to do with themselves.
Somebody's been burning circles in the grass by the Dagon shrine north of the city. The Watch is putting up notices. The Watch is always putting up notices.
Old Penhallow the apothecary had his whole case of cures stolen on the fen road. He keeps saying there's one recipe in it nobody should ever brew. Then he goes very pale and changes the subject.
legends: Wayrest was built by a merchant who bought a fishing village from its lord with a single pearl, then sold the lord the fish. The Wayresters say every coin in the city has passed through that first merchant's hands, and that if you listen at the bridges on a quiet night, you can hear the pearl rolling.

songs.title: The Fish Bridge Fiddle
lines: ~Down by the Fish Bridge the fiddlers play,
~the knights ride by at the close of day,
~the widows walk where the Lady waits,
~and the merchants count at the Bay Gate.

rumours: Young lords keep riding out to the Boethiah stones north of Daggerfall. Then they come home and their elder brothers die in duels. Strange how that keeps happening.

The Masked Revel at the Sanguine stones west of Daggerfall's still going, they say. Started at the dark of the moon. Lord Aubin Gaudrel's mother wants him home. Lord Aubin Gaudrel seems to want otherwise.
Camlorn's merchants all got rich the same summer, and none of their daughters sing any more. I'm not saying there's a connection. I'm saying I've stopped singing near Camlorn.
There's a mad poet by the Sheogorath stone south of Camlorn who rhymes better than the Count's own bard. The Count's own bard has taken it very personally.
legends: Long ago, Camlorn's dead would not stay in their graves, and walked the walls every winter night, calling the names of the living. The city's priests could do nothing. In the end a knight walked out to the bright stone south-east of the city and asked a Prince of Light for help, and the next dawn burned so fiercely that every ghost on the walls was gone. The knight was never seen again. Her shield hangs in the Dawn Chapel, and it is always warm.

rumours: Shornhelm's children are walking in their sleep, all down the same road toward the Vaermina stones. The Sheriff's asking for help. The Council's asking about the cost.
The Dowager Tamrith wants her husband's sword back from the Molag Bal shrine west of the city. She's offering a fortune. She's also offering a lecture, so be ready.
Old Archivist Haldane went to the Mora shrine and came back knowing every noble secret in Rivenspire. Half the great houses want him dead. The other half want him to dinner.
legends: Rivenspire's fogs are said to be the breath of a dragon that sleeps under the northern hills, and the great houses of Shornhelm each claim descent from a knight who once tried to wake it. None of them succeeded. All of them, in the family histories, came very close.

rumours: The bargemen won't put in at the Namira landing any more. The beggars there smile too much and ask about the cargo too closely.
Huntmaster Lorne's called off the King's autumn hunt. He says it's a bear. Bears don't stand up and open doors.
Timber's down from Evermor, cheap and plenty. The river's high and the barges are fast this year. Something's got to go wrong. It always does.
legends: The Bjoulsae, they say, was once the boundary between the lands of the Bretons and the Redguards, and a Redguard prince and a Breton princess drowned together trying to swim across it to meet. The river runs a little warmer on the night they died, and the bargemen leave two cups of wine on the bank to keep it from flooding.

rumours: King Gurak's opened Orsinium's gates to traders from Wayrest and Sentinel both. The old Orc chiefs grumble. The young ones are buying silk shirts.
Ogres in the valley below the Malacath shrine again. Orsinium's smiths walk around them like they're furniture. Furniture that eats goats.
Smugglers carry Orcish steel down the passes west of Orsinium by night and sell it to Breton lords who swear they've never bought a single Orc blade.
legends: Malacath, the Orcs say, was once the elven god Trinimac, until a trickster swallowed him and he came out changed, and his followers changed with him. The Orcs do not mourn what they were. They say they were made in the belly of a betrayal, and that is why they never forget one.

songs.title: The Forge-Song of Wrothgar
lines: ~Strike once for the mountain, strike twice for the clan,
~strike thrice for the Furious One who made us what we are;
~the snow on the anvil, the fire in the hand,
~and the blade cools hard as a grudge.

rumours: Lord Belcourt of the Old Lodge doesn't hunt by day any more. Only by night, and alone. His hounds won't come near him. His steward has started praying.
A hedge-witch near the Namira stones sells cures for the lung-rot. Works, they say. Don't ask what's in it.
Stormhaven's coast is full of old wrecks and older wreckers. If you see a lantern on the cliffs on a stormy night, don't steer toward it.
legends: Stormhaven is named, the old folk say, for a great storm that drove a fleet of Nedic ships onto its shore in the Merethic Era. The survivors married into the elves of the coast and became the first Bretons, and every great storm since has been the sea trying to take them back.

rumours: Lord Hamaad's dying in Sentinel. Lady Yasreen's ready to take the chair. Her cousin Ahzid is dining with Forebears. Everyone in the Alik'r is placing bets.
The Ashtown elves lost their moonstone lamp to sand-raiders. Their priestess walks the dunes at night looking for it. Brave, for a Dunmer. Or foolish.
The grey silk in Skaven market comes from spiders at the Mephala stones. Pretty stuff. Wear it and you start hearing other people's secrets.
Nomads say the dreams from the Vaermina stones south of Sentinel have gone bad. They dream their deaths now, and the deaths come true before the dream.
legends: Sentinel's Necropolis is older than the city, and the priests of Tu'whacca say the first Redguard king of the Alik'r is buried there with his sword across his chest. When the city is in danger, the king turns in his tomb and the sword rings, and every Ansei in Sentinel hears it in his dreams.

songs.title: The Well and the Wanderer
lines: ~Where the dunes turn red at evening and the jackals start to cry,
~there's a well of sweet water that never will run dry;
~but the man who dug it sold something he could not see,
~and his son drinks the water, and his son is not free.

rumours: The springs north of Elinhir run red and hot as blood. The Ansei rode up to look and came back without a word. That's never good.
Somebody stole the Serpent Tower's great lens in Elinhir. The mages are offering a reward. The thieves are offering a better one, to keep quiet.
Craglorn's stars move, they say. Elinhir's mages watch them every night and argue about it every day. Nobody's sure which is worse.
legends: Over Craglorn the constellations of the Celestials once came down to walk the earth: the Warrior, the Mage and the Thief, and the Serpent, which eats the others. The Elinhir astronomers still chart the Serpent's slow crawl across the sky, and on the night it reaches the Warrior's heart, they say, Craglorn will burn again.

rumours: The Ash'abah say a bone-singer's raised Old Jafar's whole caravan in the hills north of Rihad. Camels and all. You can hear the bells at night.
Old Qamar's well in Skaven was bought at the Clavicus stone. His son wants out of the bargain. Good luck to him. Princes don't refund.
Rihad's wine heirs went up to the Sanguine stones with twelve casks. They came back with a vineyard, a goat, and no memory of any of it.
legends: The Dragontail Mountains are said to be the spine of a dragon that Frandar Hunding's sword-singers slew in the first years after the Crossing. Its tail lies in the desert and its head in the sea, and the hot springs along the ridge are where its blood still runs.

rumours: Yusuf the beast-trader's tiger escaped on the Taneth quay and went north over the wall. Now it's hunting by the Hircine stones. Yusuf's offering gold. The hunters are offering prayers.
Fisherfolk vanish from the villages north of Taneth. Lord Ezhar's put a price on the slaver Iron-Collar's head. Big price. Nobody's collected.
A Taneth captain gave his ship to Sheogorath and walked inland. He's been sailing the dunes for three years. Says the wind's better there.
legends: Hew's Bane is named for Hew the Wrathful, a Ra Gada warlord who tried to conquer the peninsula and was defeated not by its warriors but by its beasts: the lions came down from the hills by night and carried off his sentries one by one until his army fled. The hunters of the Hew's Bane hills still leave the first lion skull of each season at the Huntsman's stones, to thank the beasts for their help.

rumours: The Brinewash pirates took another of Captain Noraya's ships off the south cove. The Forebears are hiring every blade on the island.
Hakim the guide will take you to the Dwemer doors in the cliffs. He won't take you through them. Ask him about his brother. Actually, don't.
They still celebrate the treaty every year on the beach. Lots of fish, lots of wine, lots of speeches about the Dominion. The speeches get longer every year.
legends: Stros M'Kai was once the seat of Prince A'tor, who fought the armies of Tiber Septim from these rocks until the last of his ships went down. The islanders say his flagship lies just off the southern cliffs, and that on still nights its lanterns burn under the water, still waiting for the order to sail.

rumours: The Red Pass Company is holding the Bangkorai road again. They'll let you through for a toll. They'll also let your enemy through, for a bigger one.
Wayrest's caravans take the Bangkorai pass now, since the bay crossings got dear. The pass is cheaper. It's also full of sellswords and old shrines.
Somebody scratched 'Captain Oriel Sand-Tongue owes me money' on the Boethiah stone. Somebody else scratched 'Not any more' underneath.
legends: Bangkorai's great fortress at the pass was built to keep the Bretons out of Hammerfell, then rebuilt to keep the Redguards out of High Rock, then rebuilt again to keep the Orcs out of both. The sentries say its stones remember every army that ever broke against them, and grumble on cold nights.

rumours: The Thalmor have a man with a book hiding in the bushes by the Peryite shrine north of Elden Root. Everyone knows he's there. He coughs.
The elders are angry about the felled graht-oak east of the city. There's talk of the old rite. My brother's a hunter. I've told him to go visit cousins in Woodhearth.
The Wood Orcs in the deep forest have stopped trading with Elden Root. They say they're tired of being called guests. They're not wrong.
legends: The great graht-oak of Elden Root was planted, the Spinners say, by Y'ffre himself on the first morning of the world, and the city grew in its branches because the Bosmer were too respectful to build on the ground and too clever to live without walls. When the tree dies, so will the Bosmer nation. The tree, the Spinners add with a smile, is in excellent health.

songs.title: The Long Road from Rimmen
lines: ~The moons are rising over Grahtwood, sugar-sweet and slow,
~the caravans are singing where the green-roofed rivers go;
~the cats will pray to Azurah and the elves will pray to none,
~and the road from Rimmen's long, my love, but the road is nearly done.

rumours: Falinesti's humming again at night. The rootkeepers say the Walking Tree's getting restless. If it walks, half the Thalmor tax-rolls walk with it.
There's a thorn-grove east of Falinesti where the trees grow bent like slaves. Molag Bal's shrine is in the middle. Warden Aldoril went in last spring. Hasn't come out.
The Kin-Breakers of Malabal Tor are holding the toll-road now. Outlaws who cut living wood. Even the Thalmor are scandalised, and the Thalmor log everything.
legends: Falinesti, the Walking Tree, once strolled across Valenwood with the seasons, wintering in the south and summering in the north, and the Bosmer of the city lived their whole lives without once setting foot on the ground. When it finally rooted, in the Third Era, the old ones wept, and said that the tree was not tired, only sad, and that it would walk again when it had something to walk toward.

rumours: Someone's burning the forest north-east of Woodhearth, one perfect circle at a time. Warden Ilthaer is hunting them. I wouldn't want to be found by Ilthaer.
The Mandate-Breakers at the Namira shrine have two net-boys from the docks. The wardens are arguing about whether the Pact allows it. The mothers aren't arguing.
Halbor the cheese-eater's still out by the Sheogorath shrine. The Spinners still can't decide if he's broken the Pact. The Silvenar's said he'll rule on it next year. Or the year after.
legends: Greenshade was the first forest Y'ffre sang, the Spinners say, and its trees still remember the tune. On certain windless nights the whole forest sways together, as if dancing, and any Bosmer who hears the song in the leaves will dream of the shape she wore before she was a Bosmer, and wake up homesick for it.

rumours: Arenthia's sleepers keep walking north to the Vaermina stones. Shazah at the Two Moons is beside herself. Her own cub walked last night.
The Silken Sisters at the Mephala shrine sell secrets to everyone: Khajiit, Bosmer, Thalmor. Doesn't matter who's buying. Everyone's betrayed by the end.
Ri'zahd the caravan-master leaves bigger offerings at the Nocturnal shrine than the thieves do. Says it's prudence. Jo'darr the thief says it's cheating.
legends: Reaper's March is named for the harvest the Khajiit and Bosmer fought over a thousand years ago, when the wheat of the border grew so tall that the two armies could not see each other and cut down their own men instead. Neither side won. The wheat was never harvested. And every year since, the people of Arenthia leave the last row of their fields uncut, for the ghosts of both armies to share.

rumours: Someone's leaving fresh blood at the Dagon shrine north of Alinor, beside the memorial to the Oblivion dead. Old Tirenwe at the Tower is furious. The Justiciars are calm. Too calm.
The crooked ones of the Namira shrine west of the city get bread from somewhere every night. The Directorate would very much like to know where.
The Lords' Hunt's been cancelled again. There's a fox in the south-west preserve. A large fox. With a family name.
There's a painter by the Sheogorath shrine who paints the Justiciars as chickens. They keep confiscating the chickens. He keeps painting.
legends: The Altmer say the first elves came ashore on Summerset from somewhere over the western sea, and that the island received them by raising the Crystal Tower overnight out of its own bedrock. The Sapiarchs do not like this tale, because it suggests the island chose the elves rather than the other way about.

songs.title: The Lamp on the Western Hill
lines: ~There's a lamp on the western hill that's burned two hundred years,
~the dead won't come to Alinor while the Lady's light is near;
~the Justiciars climbed up the hill to tell the lamp to go,
~and came back down a deal more red than when they went, you know.

rumours: Firsthold customs towed another sick ship to the quarantine anchorage. The sailors row to the Peryite shrine at night. Customs pretends not to notice. For now.
The Moth's robbed Magistrate Caladwe again. The Justiciars dug up half the hill by the Nocturnal shrine looking for her stash. All they found were moths.
The Orc dockers of Firsthold are paid half what the Altmer get. They pray to Malacath about it. Overseer Varanil has developed a rash. Coincidence, surely.
legends: Auridon was the first island of the Summerset archipelago to be settled, and Firsthold was the first city. The Altmer say the first High King built its harbour wall with his own hands, stone by stone, and that he set into it one stone that was black, so that the city would always remember that even the first and best of works has a flaw.

rumours: Artaeum came out of the fog off the western shoals again. My uncle saw a white tower and an old woman nodding at him. His nets were full. He's been unbearable since.
The Psijics take an apprentice now and then, they say, without warning. One day you're a fisherman's daughter. Next day you're gone and your mother gets a very polite letter.
The Thalmor don't like the Psijics. The Psijics don't seem to notice. That makes the Thalmor dislike them more.
legends: When the Altmer first chose to build towers and worship gods, a few among them refused, and said the Old Ways were better: to watch, to wait, to understand rather than command. Those few took ship to Artaeum and have lived there since, and the island has learned their trick of being present and absent at once. It is said that Artaeum once vanished for a whole era, and that when it came back, its monks had not noticed they were gone.

wayrest.hook: The jewel of the Iliac Bay: a merchant city of bridges, guildhalls and Breton courtesy, where the Knights of the Rose keep the peace and every honest counting-house keeps a second set of books.
wayrest.rumour: In Wayrest a man will bow to you, praise your boots and sell you a ship that sank last spring. Smile back, check your purse, and you'll do fine.

notes.title: Notice of the Wayrest Watch
notes.author: Sergeant-at-Arms Roderic Vauclain
pages:
^BY ORDER OF THE CAPTAIN OF THE WATCH
^Posted this 4th of Last Seed, 4E 201
Citizens are reminded that the old Daedric stones north of the city are NOT a feast-ground, a trysting place, nor a fit spot for wagers of courage. Three scorched circles have been found in the grass beside the shrine of the Prince of Ruin since Midyear, and one of them still had a boot in it.

Any citizen who sees torches on the north road after curfew is to report it at the Bay Gate, not to follow them. The Watch does not pay for funerals. The Watch does, however, pay five septims for a name. Discretion is assured; the Watch is, after all, Breton.

notes.title: Letter to a Partner in Elinhir
notes.author: Odile Marchand, cloth factor of the Lower Bridges
pages:
#Wayrest, 11th of Hearthfire
Dear Hassim,
Your dyed wool arrived, all forty bolts, and not one of them the colour you promised. I have sold them anyway, as 'Craglorn dusk', at a premium. The court ladies adore anything that sounds as if it came from a dangerous place. You owe me a dinner and an apology, in that order.

The bay crossing has doubled in price since the Saltreef business. The Knights of the Rose ride the docks every evening now, which is very good for my nerves and very bad for my smugglers. Send the next load overland by Bangkorai, and for pity's sake tell your drovers not to camp near the old shrines on the road. Two of Gaston's men did, last month. One came back. He has taken holy orders and will not say why.
Yours in profit,
Odile

notes.title: Handbill of Aldous Penhallow, Apothecary
notes.author: Aldous Penhallow
pages:
^REMEDIES FOR EVERY SEASON
^Penhallow's, at the Sign of the Mortar, by the Fish Bridge
Fevers broken, coughs quieted, boils lanced with a steady hand and clean steel. Tinctures of blessed thistle for the lungs. Salts of nightshade, carefully measured, for those whose sleep has fled. No charms. No curses lifted. No questions about the fen-sickness answered after dark.

Below, in a smaller and less steady hand: 'To whoever took the green-bound case from my cart on the Peryite road: keep the silver. Return the papers. There are forty years of cures in them, and one recipe I would rather no one ever read. Ask for me at the Mortar. I will not call the Watch.'

daggerfall.hook: The oldest of the Breton crowns, a grey city of towers on the Glenumbra coast where the Knights of the Dragon keep their vigils and every courtier keeps a knife behind the smile.
daggerfall.rumour: Daggerfall's court runs on whispers. You can buy a secret on the morning tide and sell it back to the same lady by supper, at a profit.

notes.title: Letter Never Sent
notes.author: Lady Ysmene Gaudrel
pages:
#Daggerfall, Turdas the 6th of Frostfall
Cousin,
You asked whether the court is quiet. It is never quiet. It is only well-mannered. This season the talk is all of young lords riding north past the Boethiah stones before dawn, swords on their hips and nothing in their saddlebags. They come back with sharper faces and fewer friends.

Sir Corwin's brother died in a duel last week over a borrowed horse. A borrowed horse! The seconds swear it was fairly fought. The seconds both wear new rings. I have begun to keep a list, and I do not like the shape it is taking.
Burn this. I mean it this time.
Y.

notes.title: A Torn Masquerade Card
pages:
^You are bidden, sweet stranger,
^to the Revel of the Ninth Mask,
^upon the first night of the dark moon,
^at the stones west of the city where the Lord of Revels keeps his chair.
Come masked. Come thirsty. Leave your name with your coachman, for you will not need it until morning, and perhaps not then.
On the back, scribbled: 'Aubin, don't you dare. Your mother will skin me. -- G.' And beneath that, in another hand: 'She'll never know.'

camlorn.hook: A proud Breton city of high walls and old ghosts in northern Glenumbra. Its merchants grow rich at a suspicious pace, and its priests of the dawn hunt what walks after dark.
camlorn.rumour: Camlorn folk will tell you their city's haunted. Then they'll tell you which ghost, and what it wants, and how much the walk costs.

notes.title: Ledger of the House Verrine
notes.author: Gilbert Verrine, wine and salt
pages:
#Accounts for Sun's Height, 4E 201
Salt from Daggerfall, 60 barrels: 480 septims. Wine sold to the Camlorn garrison: 1,120 septims. Repairs to the warehouse roof: 35 septims. Profit beyond all reasonable expectation, for the fourth month running.

Paid to the gentleman with the dog, at the stones east of the city: nothing yet.
Owed to the gentleman with the dog: one thing I do not value.
The dog says I will know what it is when it is gone. I asked if he meant the horse. The dog laughed. I did not know dogs could laugh. Lisette has stopped singing in the mornings. I am sure it is a cold.

notes.title: Sermon Notes of Brother Hugues
notes.author: Brother Hugues of the Dawn Chapel
pages: Points for Sundas: Camlorn remembers the year its dead would not stay buried. Our grandfathers did not drive them out with prayers to the Eight alone. Some of them walked to the bright stone south-east of the walls and asked a Lady of Light for help, and they got it.

Must not say that from the pulpit. The Vigilants are in town. Say instead: light is light, wherever it is lit. Say: the dead deserve rest and the living deserve courage. Say nothing of the knights who still kneel at that stone at sunrise. They know who they are.

shornhelm.hook: The black-roofed capital of Rivenspire, a city of fog, feuding noble houses and long winter nights, where the old families measure their honour in centuries and their grudges in blood.
shornhelm.rumour: Rivenspire nobles don't forgive and don't forget. They write it all down, bind it in leather, and read it to their grandchildren.

notes.title: Report of the Sheriff of Shornhelm
notes.author: Sheriff Mathis Corbeau
pages:
#To the Council of Houses, 14th of Frostfall
My lords, the sleepwalkers. I have now eleven cases, all children of the lower town, all found at dawn on the south-east road, barefoot and asleep, walking toward the old Daedric stones beyond the river. Each wakes screaming and each tells the same dream: a tower of purple glass, and a woman inside who wants to hear their stories.

The Temple says it is a fever of the season. Fevers do not walk in step. I request leave to post men at the shrine itself, and I request it before the twelfth child. If the Council will not pay for it, I will ask any capable stranger with a sword. I have already started asking.

notes.title: Letter from the Dowager of House Tamrith
notes.author: Dowager Lady Ilisande Tamrith
pages:
My dear Bertrand,
Your father's blade has not come home. The men who went to the shrine of the Lord of Chains to find him brought back his horse, his gauntlets and nothing else. They say the stones there are cold even at noon, and that there were chains on the ground, and that some of them were warm.

I will not have the family sword hanging in some Daedra's hall. It was forged when Shornhelm first raised its walls and it has never been sold, lost or surrendered. You are to do nothing foolish. You are to hire someone who does foolish things professionally. Spare no cost, but do bargain. We are Tamriths, not Montclairs.
Your mother.

evermor.hook: A quiet river city on the Bjoulsae, where barges carry timber and grain to the bay and the king's huntsmen ride out each autumn into woods that have their own opinions about who hunts whom.
evermor.rumour: Evermor's a sleepy place. Nothing happens. Well, nothing except the hunting lodge, and nobody there talks about the hunting lodge.

notes.title: Notice of the King's Huntmaster
notes.author: Gaspard Lorne, Huntmaster of Evermor
pages:
^THE AUTUMN HUNT IS SUSPENDED
By order of the Huntmaster, no party is to ride south-west of the Bjoulsae beyond the old lodge until further notice. Three hounds and a beater have been lost on the far side of the ridge, near the stones of the Huntsman Prince. The beater was found. The hounds were not.

Hunters are reminded that the prints in the mud by the ford are not a bear's, whatever the tavern says. Any man who has been bitten by any beast this season is to present himself at the lodge, quietly, and will not be punished. Any man who hides such a bite will be.

notes.title: Bargemaster's Tally
notes.author: Old Perrin of the Bjoulsae
pages: Down the river, Last Seed: oak, 30 loads. Barley, 12. One coffin for Wayrest, paid in advance, very heavy, no flowers. Up the river: salt, cloth, two priests of Stendarr who were sick over the rail the whole way.

Note to self: stop putting in at the landing below the Namira stones. Third time the beggars there have offered to buy what's in the barrels without asking what it is. Last time they asked for the coffin. Didn't like the way they asked. Didn't like the way they smiled when I said no.

orsinium.hook: The City of Orcs, rebuilt yet again in the mountains of Wrothgar by a people who have never once accepted that it should stay fallen. Its forges never cool and its gates never bow.
orsinium.rumour: Bretons have burned Orsinium more times than they can count. The Orcs have counted. Every single time. They keep the number over the gate.

notes.title: Dispatch of the Wayrest Envoy
notes.author: Sir Lucien Dorrel, envoy of the Court of Wayrest
pages:
#Orsinium, 2nd of Hearthfire, 4E 201
To His Majesty's Chancellery,
I have presented my credentials to King Gurak. He received them, read them, and used them to light his pipe. I am told this is a mark of informality rather than contempt. I am told a great many things here, chiefly by large people standing too close.

The city is larger than our maps admit, its walls thicker, its smiths more numerous. The Hall of the Clans shouts more and decides faster than our own council ever has. I recommend, with respect, that the Crown abandon any notion of a punitive expedition and instead purchase as many Orcish blades as the forgemasters will sell. I have already bought three. For the Crown, naturally.

notes.title: Order Book of the Third Forge
notes.author: Rugdash gra-Lurz, smith
pages: Axe heads, 40, for the Bloodfist clan. Paid. Breastplates, 12, for a Redguard captain from Bangkorai. Paid in good gold, half of it bitten by me. Horseshoes, 200, for the Breton envoy. He asked for them 'with fewer spikes'. Made them with fewer spikes. Charged extra for the disappointment.

Took the first blade of the new ore to the shrine south-west of the city, as my mother did and hers before. Laid it on the stone and left it. Did not look back. The Furious One does not like smiths who look back at what they have given. The ogres were thick in the valley again. Walked around them. A smith's arms are for the hammer.

notes.title: Tablet by the Gate of Orsinium
pages:
~Here stood the city. Here it fell.
~Here stood the city again.
~Count the fallings, stranger, and then count the risings,
~and know which number is larger.

Beneath, scratched by many hands in many years: notches. Rows of them. Someone has carved a last notch, deeper than the rest, beside the newest gatestone, and beneath it in plain letters: NOT THIS TIME. A Breton visitor once asked a gate-guard what the notches meant. The guard said they were a tally of lessons. The visitor asked who had been taught. The guard only smiled, and showed him the gate, and told him the toll had just gone up.

shrine_azura_high_rock.hook: A slender stone of Azura on the hills north-west of Wayrest, where Breton widows come at the turning of the light to ask the Queen of Dusk and Dawn for one more glimpse of what they have lost.
shrine_azura_high_rock.rumour: The rose-widows of Wayrest walk out to the Azura stone every evening. They say the Lady shows you a dream of your dead if you sit still long enough. I'd rather not sit that still.

notes.title: The Dusk-Book of the Rose Widows
pages:
^Written in many hands, in a calf-bound book chained to the stone
~Lady of the in-between, of the hour the lamps are lit,
~I do not ask you for him back. I know the bargain of the world.
~I ask only to see his face once at dusk, as he looked
~coming up the Fish Bridge with the catch, before the fever.

-- Margaux, 3rd of Sun's Dawn. She showed me. He was laughing.

Lady, my son sailed for Stros M'Kai and the sea took him. Let me know only whether he was afraid. -- Hélène, 19th of Rain's Hand.

She showed me a ship's lantern, burning steady. I choose to believe it means no. -- H.
Do not write here unless you mean it. The Lady reads every word and she remembers the liars. -- A widow of thirty years.

shrine_boethiah_high_rock.hook: A dark shrine of Boethiah on the Glenumbra heath north of Daggerfall. Ambitious young lords ride out to it before dawn, and the duels fought there end with a funeral and a promotion.
shrine_boethiah_high_rock.rumour: They say if you want your elder brother's title in Daggerfall, you go pray at the Boethiah stone. Then you wait for him to insult the wrong swordsman. It never takes long.

notes.title: An Unsigned Compact
pages:
^Compact of the Unbound, sworn before the Prince of Plots
I, who am second-born, swear that I will no longer be second. I will take what the accident of birth denied me, and I will take it by the old Breton right, steel in the morning mist, so that no court can name it murder. The Unbound will supply the champion. I will supply the insult.

In payment I give to the Prince the blood of my brother and the faith of all who trusted him. The champion of the Unbound, Sir Brayan Ferrec, keeps his vigil at this stone each night until the matter is concluded.
The next name on our list is that of Lady Gaudrel's brother-in-law. Then the Lady herself, if she keeps asking questions.

shrine_clavicus_vile_high_rock.hook: A smiling shrine of Clavicus Vile in the fields east of Camlorn. Camlorn merchants deny ever visiting it, and yet the path to it is worn as smooth as a guildhall stair.
shrine_clavicus_vile_high_rock.rumour: Half the rich men of Camlorn got rich in a single season. Ask how, and they say 'shrewd investment'. Ask where they invested, and they look east and go quiet.

notes.title: A Merchant's Regret
notes.author: Gilbert Verrine
pages:
To whatever reads letters left at this stone,
I asked for prosperity and you gave it. Every venture has turned to gold. The salt sells before it lands. The wine sells before it is pressed. My rivals go bankrupt in their sleep. I have bought the house on the hill with the blue shutters that my father could only look at.

My daughter Lisette does not sing any more. She does not laugh. She does her lessons and eats her supper and looks at me as if I were a stranger who has paid for her board. Your dog said I would lose one thing I did not value. I did not know I did not value it until it was gone.
Take the house back. Take the gold. I am told that is not how this works. I am leaving this letter anyway.

shrine_hermaeus_mora_high_rock.hook: A shrine of Hermaeus Mora in the misty hills south of Shornhelm, ringed by stones carved with eyes. Rivenspire scholars who come to it seeking one answer tend to leave with too many.
shrine_hermaeus_mora_high_rock.rumour: The old archivist of Shornhelm went to the Mora stone to learn who poisoned his patron. He learned. Then he learned everything else, and now he doesn't sleep.

notes.title: Journal of the Archivist of House Montclair
notes.author: Archivist Dorien Haldane
pages:
#Second Seed, the 9th
The Montclair archives are silent on the death of Lord Bastien. I have read every ledger, every letter, every laundry list. Someone has cut the pages I need with a very sharp knife. There is one library in Rivenspire that no one can cut. I am going to the stones south of the city tomorrow.

#Second Seed, the 10th
I asked. The eyes in the stone opened. I was shown the name of the poisoner, and the name of the man who paid him, and the name of the man who paid him, and so on back, house by house, three hundred years. Every noble line in Rivenspire is in it. Every one.

#Second Seed, the 30th
I have not slept. I cannot stop knowing. It is very quiet in my head now, except for the pages turning. I think the pages are turning me.

shrine_hircine_high_rock.hook: A shrine of Hircine in the Stormhaven woods south-west of Evermor, hung with antlers and old hunting horns. The king's huntsmen avoid it; something that wears a man's face does not.
shrine_hircine_high_rock.rumour: Huntmaster Lorne's lost three hounds and a beater by the Hircine stone. He says it's a bear. He's an honest man, Gaspard. That's why he can't lie well.

notes.title: Tally of the Old Lodge
notes.author: Hugo Morel, steward of the Old Lodge
pages:
^Kills of the Old Lodge, offered at the Stone of the Huntsman
Sun's Dawn: one stag, twelve tines, taken by Lord Remy on foot. Rain's Hand: a boar, a brace of hares, a Reachman poacher (accidental; regretted; reported). Midyear: one bear, taken by Lord Remy with a knife, after which his lordship was abed nine days.

Sun's Height: his lordship hunted alone, by night, and brought back nothing that he would name. Hearthfire: his lordship asks that we no longer bolt the kennel. The hounds have begun to howl when he comes near. I have written to Huntmaster Lorne at Evermor. I do not know what else a steward is to do.

shrine_malacath_high_rock.hook: A brutal shrine of Malacath in the crags south-west of Orsinium, where Orc smiths lay the first blade of every new ore and Orc warriors come to be reminded of the Code, whether they like it or not.
shrine_malacath_high_rock.rumour: Orsinium's smiths walk out to the Malacath shrine with a new blade and walk home without it. Ogres in that valley, mind. The smiths say the ogres are part of the test.

notes.title: Words Scratched on an Offered Blade
notes.author: Rugdash gra-Lurz
pages:
~Furious One, Lord of the Spurned,
~this is the first edge of the new seam.
~I did not make it beautiful. I made it true.
~Take it, and keep the next one sharp in my hand.

Scratched along the fuller in a smaller hand: 'Mother said you hear us best when we are angry. I am angry that the Bretons still call us beasts. I am angry that the ore runs thin. I am angry that my son wants to be a poet. Hear me, then. And if you could make the boy rhyme a little better, I would not complain.'

shrine_mehrunes_dagon_high_rock.hook: A spiked shrine of Mehrunes Dagon on the hills north of Wayrest, ringed by scorched circles in the grass. Someone in the city has been praying for ruin, and doing it in company.
shrine_mehrunes_dagon_high_rock.rumour: The Watch found a boot in one of those burnt circles north of town. Just a boot. Good leather, too. Wayrest cut, by the stitching.

notes.title: Scorched Pamphlet
pages:
^THE CITY OF COINS SHALL BURN
Brothers and sisters of the Ember, Wayrest has grown fat on other men's labour. Its bridges are built on debts and its guilds on lies. The Prince of Ruin does not hate the city. He only wishes to show it what it already is: kindling.

We meet at the stone on the dark of each moon. Bring a coal from your own hearth. Bring the name of one who has wronged you. You will not need to bring anything else. The Ember provides.
(Below, half burnt away:) ...the Bay Gate warehouses, on the night of the Merchants' Feast, when the Knights are all at table...

notes.title: Scrawl on a Guard's Shield
notes.author: Watchman Alard
pages: Left here by Watchman Alard, 21st of Sun's Height. Followed four torches up from the north road like a fool. Counted eleven of them at the stone in red hoods. Heard them talk of the Merchants' Feast. Heard one say the name 'Corvane', which is a guild name.

They saw me. I am behind the rocks east of the shrine and my leg is no good. If anyone finds this before they find me, tell the Sergeant-at-Arms: it isn't beggars and it isn't madmen. It's guildsmen. Tell him to check the Feast list.

shrine_mephala_high_rock.hook: A shrine of Mephala on the heath north-east of Daggerfall, its stones strung with silk threads tied in knots. Every knot is a secret someone left in trade for another.
shrine_mephala_high_rock.rumour: At the Webspinner's stone outside Daggerfall you tie a knot and whisper a secret into it. Next morning you know one of somebody else's. That's how the court got the way it is.

notes.title: Ledger of Knots
pages:
^Kept by the Keeper of Threads, for the Mother of Whispers
Red knot: the Duchess of the Northern Wing has paid her gambling debts with her husband's signet. Traded for: the name of the Duke's mistress.
Blue knot: the Captain of the Harbour sells the Dragon Knights' sailing dates. Traded for: the name of the man who buys them.
Black knot: Lady Gaudrel keeps a list. Traded for: who is on it.

Green knot: the Lord Commander knows nothing of any of this. He is the only honest man at court and therefore the most dangerous. Traded for: nothing yet. No one has a secret worth so much.
Every knot is a strand. Every strand is a web. Pull gently.

shrine_meridia_high_rock.hook: A bright shrine of Meridia south-east of Camlorn, where knights of the old city still kneel at sunrise and swear to give the restless dead the rest that Camlorn once could not.
shrine_meridia_high_rock.rumour: Camlorn knights pray at the Meridia stone before they go after a haunting. The priests pretend not to know. Saves everyone a great deal of ink.

notes.title: Oath of the Dawnward Knights
pages:
~Lady of the bright edge, of the light that will not bend,
~we were the city that could not bury its dead.
~We remember the winter the mourners walked the walls,
~and the morning you broke it.

~Lend me the light for one more night.
~What rises without leave, I will put down.
~What is bound against its will, I will cut loose.
~And when I fall, let me fall facing the sunrise.
^Sworn by Dame Clemence Varre, Sir Odo of the Wall, and eleven whose names the wind has taken.

shrine_molag_bal_high_rock.hook: A shrine of Molag Bal in the cold hills west of Shornhelm, strewn with rusted chains. A lord of House Tamrith rode out to burn it and never came home; his ancestral sword is still somewhere inside the circle.
shrine_molag_bal_high_rock.rumour: Lord Tamrith went to cleanse the Molag Bal shrine and the shrine cleansed him. They say his sword's still there, stuck in the stone, and that something sits beside it and waits for the next fool.

notes.title: Scratched on a Shackle-Stone
pages: My name is Etienne Coste. I am a groom of House Tamrith. I rode with my lord to burn this place. My lord is dead. They kept me because they wanted someone to watch.

There are four of us left. The Lady of Chains feeds every third night. She wears my lord's ring on a thread around her neck and she keeps his sword in the stone like a trophy. She says no one will come. Tell the Dowager we tried. Tell her the sword is here. Tell her to send someone who is not afraid of the cold.

shrine_namira_high_rock.hook: A shrine of Namira by a Bjoulsae landing in Stormhaven, tended by beggars, lepers and the unloved of three cities. They are kind to strangers. They are unusually curious about what strangers are carrying.
shrine_namira_high_rock.rumour: The Namira beggars by the river landing won't take your coin. They want your leftovers. All your leftovers. Some say they're not fussy what kind.

notes.title: Hymn of the Unlovely
pages:
~Lady of the spider and the slug, of the cellar and the sore,
~the bright folk of Evermor do not look at us.
~So be it. We look at them.
~We see them throw away their bread, their cloth, their old men.

~We take what they throw away, and we give thanks.
~We are the mouth at the end of the world.
~Nothing is wasted while we live,
~and when we die, Lady, nothing will be wasted then either.
^Kept at the river landing by Mother Crell, who has not been warm since Sun's Dusk of 4E 170.

shrine_nocturnal_high_rock.hook: A shadowed shrine of Nocturnal in the Wrothgar foothills west of Orsinium, a waypoint for smugglers who carry Orcish steel to Breton buyers who would rather not be seen buying it.
shrine_nocturnal_high_rock.rumour: Smugglers leave a coin for the Night Mistress at that shrine west of Orsinium before they cross the passes. The ones who forget don't usually make it to Evermor.

notes.title: A Smuggler's Route Card
notes.author: Black Tomas
pages: For the crew, in case I don't come back from Orsinium. You know the route: shrine to the Malacath crags, crags to the river, river to Evermor, no lanterns, no songs. Leave the Mistress her coin. Always the coin.

The Breton factor stiffed us on the last run, so I kept the twelve finest blades back as surety. They're under the flat black stone south-east of the shrine, about twenty paces out, wrapped in oilcloth with a crow feather tied to the bundle. If I'm dead, sell them. If I'm alive, and you've touched them, I'll know.

shrine_peryite_high_rock.hook: A sickly shrine of Peryite in the fens north-east of Wayrest, where plague-penitents come to beg the Taskmaster for a cure, or for a curse to send downriver to someone else.
shrine_peryite_high_rock.rumour: Old Penhallow the apothecary had his case of cures stolen on the fen road by the Peryite stone. He says there's a recipe in it nobody should brew. He says it like he's brewed it.

notes.title: Notes of the Tender of the Pox
notes.author: Velmont, called the Tender
pages: The old fool's case is a treasure. Forty years of fevers, catalogued, cured and, in the last pages, reversed. He found how the Knahaten sickness might be woken from dust. Then he lost his nerve and wrote 'NEVER' across it in red. Cowards always write in red.

The Taskmaster is pleased with us. He likes order, and nothing is so orderly as a plague: it takes the weak first, the proud second, and leaves the rest to sweep up. We will brew the first measure here at the shrine on the next dark moon and send it downriver to Wayrest in the fish barrels. The Lower Bridges will learn humility.

shrine_sanguine_high_rock.hook: A shrine of Sanguine in the woods west of Daggerfall, where masked Breton nobles hold revels that last three days and are discussed for three years. Not every guest comes home.
shrine_sanguine_high_rock.rumour: Young Lord Aubin Gaudrel went to a masked revel by the Sanguine stones and hasn't been seen since. His mother is pretending she isn't frantic. She's very good at it, and it isn't working.

notes.title: Guest Book of the Ninth Mask
pages:
^Sign with your mask, not your name
The Grinning Fox: came for the wine, stayed for the wager.
The Gilded Owl: lost my wife's pearls to a dremora at dice. Worth it.
The Weeping Moon: has anyone seen my coachman?
The Silver Stag (in a young, careful hand): just a cup or two, then home before Mother wakes.

The Silver Stag (the same hand, much later, much less careful): The host says I can win back the signet if I play one more round. The host has such kind red eyes. I do not think I will be home before Mother wakes. I do not think I will be home at all. It is the best night of my life.

shrine_sheogorath_high_rock.hook: A crooked shrine of Sheogorath in the Glenumbra meadows south-west of Camlorn, decorated by its devotees with spoons, cheese rinds and some genuinely excellent poetry.
shrine_sheogorath_high_rock.rumour: There's a poet camps at the Sheogorath stone south of Camlorn. Says the Mad God writes his verses for him. They're better than the court poet's. That's what worries people.

notes.title: Verses Nailed to a Fence-Post
notes.author: Gilles the Unbuttoned
pages:
~I asked the Lord of Madness for a rhyme,
~he gave me nine, and took away the time.
~Now Turdas comes on Sundas twice a week,
~and all my spoons are learning how to speak.

~The Count of Camlorn wears a cheese for crown;
~I told him so. He would not take it down.
~O Breton lords, so certain, proud and wise,
~it's you he laughs at, wearing my disguise.
^(Below:) Leave cheese. Leave spoons. Leave anything you are too sure of. -- G.

shrine_vaermina_high_rock.hook: A shrine of Vaermina across the river south-east of Shornhelm. Since autumn, children of the lower town have been sleepwalking toward it in the night, all dreaming the same purple dream.
shrine_vaermina_high_rock.rumour: The sleepwalking children of Shornhelm all walk the same road, toward the Vaermina stones. The Sheriff's asking for swords. The Temple's asking for calm. I'm asking for a lock on my door.

notes.title: Diary of the Dream-Keeper
notes.author: Sister Oriane, formerly of the Temple of Shornhelm
pages:
#Frostfall the 2nd
The nobles of Shornhelm will not pay me for their dreams any longer. Very well. Children dream more freely, and more honestly, and in such vivid colours. The Mistress of the Orb is delighted with them.

#Frostfall the 9th
The eleventh child walked all the way to the stone before her mother caught her. Such a lovely dream: she was a queen of a drowned city, and everyone she loved was a fish. I took the dream and left her the fear. That is the tithe. The Sheriff has started asking questions. The Mistress says I should give him a dream of his own.

sentinel.hook: The great harbour-city of the Alik'r coast, seat of the Crowns, where an old lord lies dying in his palace and every faction in Hammerfell has come to watch which way the chair will fall.
sentinel.rumour: Lord Hamaad's failing. The Crowns say Lady Yasreen will hold Sentinel. The Forebears smile and say nothing. When a Forebear smiles in Sentinel, check the harbour for new ships.

notes.title: Harbourmaster's Ledger
notes.author: Rashida at-Kesh, Harbourmistress of Sentinel
pages:
#Week of the 8th of Hearthfire, 4E 201
In: four dhows from Taneth (Forebear cargo, inspected twice, as His Lordship's nephew asked me not to). Two Breton cogs from Wayrest, cloth and wine. One Altmer sloop, turned away at the mole. The Dominion has not been welcome in this harbour since the treaty and I do not intend to be the one who forgets it.

Ashtown, the Dunmer quarter behind the fish market, asks again for leave to keep night lamps burning on the south road. Their priestess walks out to the old Azura stone in the dunes each dusk and the lamps guide her home. Leave granted. They have paid their harbour dues without complaint for thirty years. That is more than I can say for the Forebears.

notes.title: Teaching of the Priest of Tu'whacca
notes.author: Arkhan at-Sentinel, keeper of the Necropolis gate
pages: Children of the Crowns, remember: Tu'whacca keeps the road for the dead, and the road must be clean. We wash our dead. We wrap them. We sing them across the desert to the Far Shores. We do not leave them for the jackal or the vulture, and we do not leave them for the ones who live by the Namira stone in the dunes south-west of the city.

Some of you have given those people bread. That is kindness and I do not forbid it. But when a beggar of the stone asks you whether any old ones in your household are sickly, do not answer. Close your door. Come and tell me. The dead are owed their journey, and some in this land would cut it short for a meal.

notes.title: Letter from an Old Crown Captain
notes.author: Captain Imani at-Rasad, retired
pages:
Daughter,
You ask why I will not sit at the Forebear table at your wedding. I will sit. I will eat. I will even dance, if my knee permits. But I marched from Sentinel to the Alik'r wells in the war against the Dominion, and I watched the Forebears in Taneth and Rihad count their profits while the Crowns counted their dead. When the Emperor signed us away to the elves, it was not the merchants who drove the elves out.

That is old dust now. Hammerfell is free and stands alone, and I am glad of it. Marry your Forebear boy. He has good teeth and a kind mother. Only teach your children the names of the dead before you teach them the price of silk.

elinhir.hook: A city of mages and star-watchers on the edge of Craglorn, whose towers hold observatories older than the Empire and whose scholars argue, very loudly, about what the constellations are about to do.
elinhir.rumour: Elinhir's mages say the Craglorn stars move when nobody's looking. Then they all stay up looking. Nobody in that city has slept properly in a hundred years.

notes.title: Complaint of the Observatory of Elinhir
notes.author: Magister Hadiya Sel-Nur, Keeper of the Lenses
pages:
#To the Lord Warden of Elinhir, 23rd of Last Seed
My lord, for the third time: the great lens of the Serpent Tower has been stolen. It was ground by Yokudan glassmakers before the Crossing. It cannot be replaced, and without it we cannot chart the Serpent's movement through the Craglorn sky this winter.

The thieves were seen heading south toward the shrine of the Night Mistress beyond the city. Everyone in Elinhir knows the thieves' crews of Craglorn make their offerings there. Everyone, it appears, except the Watch. If the Watch will not fetch it back, I will pay whoever does. I will pay handsomely. I will even stop complaining, for a season.

notes.title: Caravan Notice at the North Gate
notes.author: The Caravan-Masters of Elinhir
pages:
^TO ALL DROVERS ON THE WAYREST ROAD
Do not water your beasts at the springs north of the city below the spiked shrine. Two caravans have found the water hot as a kettle and red as a wound, and a third has not been found at all.

The Ansei of the Crowns rode up last week and came back silent. They have asked the Lord Warden for fire-wards and twenty more swords. Until the springs run clear, take the long road by Bangkorai. It costs three days. It is cheaper than a funeral.

skaven.hook: A walled oasis city of the Alik'r interior, rich in silk and water, where the wells are worth more than gold and an old family once bought theirs from someone who was not quite a man.
skaven.rumour: Every family in Skaven owns a well, a grudge, or both. The Qamar family's well never runs dry. People ask why. The Qamars stop smiling.

notes.title: Letter of the Silk-Weavers of Skaven
notes.author: Mistress Zainab, of the Weavers' Court
pages:
Sister,
The new silk from the south-east is finer than anything from the coast. Too fine. It is grey as smoke and it does not tear, and the girl who brings it will not say where she gets it. I followed her. She walks out past the walls to the old Webspinner's stones and comes back with a bolt each week and a new secret each day.

She knows things about the Weavers' Court that only the Court should know. She knows which of us cheats on the dye-tax. She smiles when she passes my stall. I have stopped buying her silk. The others have not. Come home, sister, and bring a sharper sword than mine.

notes.title: Report of the Well-Warden
notes.author: Musa the Well-Warden
pages: Wells of the East Quarter, Hearthfire count: eleven dry, four brackish, one sweet. The sweet one is the Qamar well, as ever. It has never dropped a hand's breadth in forty years, not even in the drought of 4E 189 when we buried the camels.

Old Qamar the elder bought that well, they say, from a smiling man with a dog at the shrine east of the city. The price was 'nothing of value to him.' His wife left him the same summer. His son, Qamar the younger, sells the water now and does not sleep. I note this only because the Warden's office is asked to report anything unusual about the wells. This is unusual.

rihad.hook: A Forebear trading city on the Gold Coast border, rich in wine and wagons, where the Ash'abah watch the sands for the walking dead and the merchants watch the road to Cyrodiil for buyers.
rihad.rumour: Rihad wine's the best in Hammerfell, and the Rihad dead are the worst. The Ash'abah say the bone-singers have come back to the hills north of town. Drink while you can.

notes.title: Letter from an Ash'abah Warrior
notes.author: Daria of the Ash'abah
pages:
Brother,
The city still will not let us inside the walls after dark. They buy our protection by day and bar the gate against us by night, as if the smell of the grave were on us. Let them. We camp at the bright stone north of the city, where the Lady of Light keeps her shrine, and we watch.

There is a bone-singer in the hills. He has raised the caravan of Old Jafar, every camel and drover of it, and walks them in circles under the moon. Worse: he has dug up an Ansei. One of the old sword-singers, buried with his blade. The blade sings for the necromancer now. Come quickly. Bring salt.

notes.title: Ledger of the Saffron Press
notes.author: Barid at-Rihad, vintner
pages: Pressed this season: 400 casks of the red, 120 of the gold. Sold to Kvatch: 90. Sold to Anvil: 160. Sold to Lord Ezhar's agents in Taneth: everything else, at a price that made me weep.

Missing: 12 casks of the gold, the very best, taken from the cellar by my own son and carried north-east to the Sanguine shrine for some revel. He came back on the third day with no shoes, a goat, and a deed to a vineyard in Cyrodiil he does not remember winning. The deed is genuine. The goat will not leave.

taneth.hook: The proud harbour of the Forebears on the Hew's Bane coast, crowded with dhows, warehouses and beast-markets, where Lord Ezhar's merchants deal with all the world and ask no questions of its coin.
taneth.rumour: Taneth sells anything: silk, steel, tigers. Somebody sold a tiger last month that didn't stay sold. It's out there north of the walls now, and it remembers the man with the whip.

notes.title: Journal of a Beast-Trader
notes.author: Yusuf the Tamer
pages:
#Frostfall the 3rd
The great senche from Elsweyr broke her cage on the quay last night. Old Saffron, the dock boys call her: twice the size of a horse and the colour of ripe dates. She killed my best handler and went over the north wall like a cat over a fence.

#Frostfall the 9th
She has been seen near the Hircine stones north of the city, where the Hew's Bane hunters leave skulls. She is eating goats. Soon she will stop eating goats. Lord Ezhar's steward says the fine for an escaped beast is my whole stock. I would rather pay a hunter. I would rather pay a hunter a great deal.

notes.title: Notice of the Forebear Harbour Court
notes.author: Harbour Court of Taneth
pages:
^BY ORDER OF LORD EZHAR AT-TANETH
The trade in persons is forbidden in this harbour and in all of Hew's Bane. Any captain found carrying shackled passengers will forfeit his ship, his cargo and his right hand.

It has come to the Court's notice that persons are nonetheless being taken from the fishing villages north of the city and marched inland to the shrine of the Lord of Chains, where they are sold to buyers who come over the hills by night. The Court offers two hundred gold for the name of the slaver called Iron-Collar. The Court offers more for his head.

stros_mkai.hook: A rocky island town off the Hammerfell coast, where the old treaty that freed Hammerfell from the Dominion was signed, and where Dwemer ruins and pirate coves are both just a short and dangerous walk away.
stros_mkai.rumour: Stros M'Kai's where Hammerfell told the Dominion to go home. Proudest rock in the sea. Mind the pirates on the far side, though. They don't read treaties.

notes.title: Handbill of Hakim the Guide
notes.author: Hakim, Guide to the Ruins
pages:
^SEE THE WONDERS OF THE DEEP FOLK!
Hakim, born on this very rock, will lead visitors to the brass doors of the old Dwemer halls in the cliffs. The walk includes lantern, rope, bread, and a short and very moving speech about the treaty. Price negotiable. Bravery not included.

Note: Hakim does not go INSIDE. Hakim has been inside. Hakim's brother went further inside. Hakim does not have a brother any more. Gentlemen of learning who wish to go inside may do so at their own expense, and are asked to settle their bill first.

notes.title: Letter of a Stros M'Kai Fisherwife
notes.author: Samira of the Hook Quay
pages:
Mother,
The catch is good and the prices are poor, which is how the gods like it. The Brinewash pirates took another of Captain Noraya's ships last week off the south cove. Now nobody from Taneth will sail here without an escort, and the escorts eat more fish than they guard.

I am sending the girls to you in Sentinel on the next grain boat. It is only until the Forebears deal with the pirates, or the pirates deal with the Forebears. I do not much care which. Tell Grandfather not to teach them any more Yokudan curses. The little one used one on the priest.

shrine_azura_hammerfell.hook: A shrine of Azura among the dunes south of Sentinel, kept by Dunmer whose grandparents fled the Red Year. Their lamp of moonstone has burned here for seventy years, until raiders took it last month.
shrine_azura_hammerfell.rumour: The Ashtown elves walk to the Azura stone every dusk and every dawn. Sand-raiders stole their moonstone lamp. Priestess Nerevi's been out there praying in the dark ever since.

notes.title: Prayer of the Ashtown Exiles
notes.author: Nerevi Andrano, priestess of Ashtown
pages:
~Mother of the Rose, Queen of the in-between hour,
~your mountain burned and your children ran.
~We crossed the whole of Tamriel with ash in our hair,
~and in this land of sand and strangers we set your stone again.

My grandmother carried the moonstone lamp from Ebonheart on her back. It burned on this stone every night since. Last month it was taken by sand-raiders from the Alik'r who camp in the dunes south of here. They want gold for it. I have no gold. I have only you, Lady, and you have always preferred that we help ourselves.
If a stranger reads this: I am in Sentinel, in Ashtown, behind the fish market. Bring her light home.

shrine_boethiah_hammerfell.hook: A shrine of Boethiah high in the Bangkorai pass between Wayrest and Elinhir, where sellsword companies swear blood-oaths before a war and settle their mutinies after one.
shrine_boethiah_hammerfell.rumour: The Red Pass Company took its oaths at the Boethiah stone in Bangkorai. Forty swords went in. Thirty-one came out. The other nine are buried under the shrine, and they were the officers.

notes.title: Muster Roll of the Red Pass Company
notes.author: Captain Oriel Sand-Tongue
pages:
^We who sign here, Redguard, Breton, Orc and one very angry Nord, swear before the Prince of the Knife:
To hold the pass for whoever pays, until they stop paying. To take what is owed from employers who forget. To follow the captain while the captain wins, and to replace the captain the moment the captain loses.

Signed by forty marks, crosses and one drawing of a goat.
Added later, in red: Captain Hessa lost at Fallen Grotto. Replaced. Captain Brannoc lost his nerve. Replaced. Captain Oriel Sand-Tongue holds the roll. She sleeps with her back to the wall and her eyes half open, which is the only way the Prince approves of.

shrine_clavicus_vile_hammerfell.hook: A grinning shrine of Clavicus Vile in the scrubland east of Skaven, where a desperate man once traded for a well that never runs dry. His son still sells the water, and still owes the debt.
shrine_clavicus_vile_hammerfell.rumour: The Qamar well in Skaven was bought at the Clavicus stone. Old Qamar paid with 'something of no value'. Young Qamar thinks that something was his own soul. He'd like it back.

notes.title: Contract of the Sweet Well
pages:
^Agreed upon this 1st of Midyear, 4E 161, between Qamar son of Hafiz, well-digger of Skaven, and a Prince of Bargains, by proxy of his faithful hound.
The Prince grants: a well in the East Quarter of Skaven that shall never run dry so long as the house of Qamar holds it.

Qamar grants: the thing that is of no value to him, to be collected at the Prince's convenience, from him or his heirs.
The original lies sealed in the shrine, under the dog's paw. The house of Qamar keeps no copy, for the house of Qamar was not given one. Note, in the margin, in a newer hand: 'Father, what did you think you were worth?'

shrine_hermaeus_mora_hammerfell.hook: A shrine of Hermaeus Mora in the hills north-west of Rihad, where Redguard scholars come in search of the lost maps of drowned Yokuda and come back fluent in tongues no one has spoken in an age.
shrine_hermaeus_mora_hammerfell.rumour: A Rihad scholar went to the Mora shrine asking where old Yokuda sank. Came back reciting the names of every ship of the Crossing. He can't stop. His wife's moved to her sister's.

notes.title: Journal of a Seeker of Yokuda
notes.author: Tariq al-Hazir of Rihad
pages:
#Sun's Height, the 2nd
Every Redguard child is told the land of our ancestors sank into the sea. No Redguard scholar has ever been told where. Our maps begin with the Crossing and end with the shore. I am tired of beginning at the shore.

#Sun's Height, the 5th
The Lord of Knowledge answered. He showed me Yokuda under the waves, its towers drowned in green light. He showed me the Hiradirge, the old sword-singers' halls. He showed me where the Ra Gada first set out. He showed me the way back.

#Sun's Height, the 6th
He asked for my name in exchange. Not the word. The thing. I did not understand. I said yes. My wife called me this morning by my name and I did not turn my head.

shrine_hircine_hammerfell.hook: A shrine of Hircine in the dry hills north of Taneth, piled with the skulls of lions and jackals left by the hunters of Hew's Bane. Lately the skulls have been joined by bones that nobody left.
shrine_hircine_hammerfell.rumour: Hew's Bane hunters say the Huntsman's sent them a beast: the escaped tiger from Yusuf's cages. They're laying bets on who'll take her skin. Yusuf's betting on the tiger.

notes.title: Words Cut Around a Lion Skull
pages:
~Father of the Hunt, Lord of the Dry Grass,
~here is the lion of the Hew's Bane hills.
~I took him with a spear, as the old way asks.
~I did not take him from behind.

Cut beneath, by another hand, deeper and fresher: 'Father of the Hunt, the great cat from Elsweyr has come to your stones and the city men want her dead with poison and nets. That is no hunt. Give her to a hunter worthy of her, or let her go free. -- Malik of the Hills, who has seen her drink at the dry well at dawn.'

shrine_malacath_hammerfell.hook: A shrine of Malacath in the rocky waste east of Sentinel, kept by Orc swords-for-hire whom Hammerfell paid to fight its wars and then forgot to thank.
shrine_malacath_hammerfell.rumour: The Orcs east of Sentinel fought for the Crowns against the Dominion. Then the war ended and the Crowns stopped answering their letters. They've stopped writing letters. Now they pray.

notes.title: Oath of the Unpaid
notes.author: Ghorza gra-Bagol, captain of the Iron Wells band
pages:
~Malacath, we held the wells of the Alik'r for the Crowns.
~We bled for them at the Dominion line.
~They promised land when the elves were gone.
~The elves are gone. The land is not ours.

We do not ask you to curse the Crowns. Curses are for the weak. We ask you to remember, as we remember. Every Orc of the Iron Wells band who dies in Hammerfell's service is named here, cut in the stone, so that when the Crowns forget, the stone will not.
There are eighty-one names. There is room for more. We have checked.

shrine_mehrunes_dagon_hammerfell.hook: A spiked shrine of Mehrunes Dagon in the Craglorn hills north of Elinhir, where the springs have begun to boil and caravans to vanish. The Ansei of the Crowns came back from it silent.
shrine_mehrunes_dagon_hammerfell.rumour: The springs below the Dagon shrine north of Elinhir run red and hot now. My cousin swears he saw a gate of fire open in the rocks for a heartbeat. He's a liar, my cousin. He's also gone very pale.

notes.title: Report of an Ansei Scout
notes.author: Jamila, sword-singer of the Crowns
pages:
#To the Lord Warden of Elinhir, Frostfall
The shrine of the Destroyer is in use. Fresh ash on the altar, fresh blood on the spikes. Seven cultists in red, Breton and Redguard both, singing in a tongue that made my teeth ache. When they sang, the spring below the shrine boiled.

I did not engage. The Shehai would not come to my hand there. That has never happened to me. The spirit-sword simply would not form, as if something in the stones drank it. I recommend fire-wards, priests of Stendarr, and twenty swords of plain steel. Mine will not do this time.

shrine_mephala_hammerfell.hook: A shrine of Mephala in the hot rocks south-east of Skaven, its stones veiled in grey spider-silk finer than any loom in the Alik'r could weave, and worth more than its weight in secrets.
shrine_mephala_hammerfell.rumour: That grey silk in Skaven market comes from the Webspinner's stones. Wear it and you hear whispers. Sell it and you hear more. The Weavers' Court is tearing itself apart.

notes.title: Thread-Wrapped Letter
notes.author: Lalah, who brings the silk
pages: Mother of Webs, the Weavers' Court of Skaven called me a beggar's girl and spat in my bowl. Now they buy my silk with both hands and every bolt carries one of your whispers into their houses. Mistress Zainab cheats the dye-tax. Master Rahim's wife is not his wife. The Court's treasurer has a second family in Rihad.

I do not sell their secrets, Mother. Not yet. I only let them know I know. It is so much sweeter to watch them wonder. When they are all quite frightened, I will ask for a seat on the Court. And they will give it, and they will smile, and they will never sleep again. Thank you for the spiders.

shrine_meridia_hammerfell.hook: A shining shrine of Meridia in the hills north of Rihad, where the Ash'abah, Hammerfell's outcast hunters of the dead, keep their camp. A bone-singer is loose in the hills, and he has woken an Ansei.
shrine_meridia_hammerfell.rumour: The Ash'abah camp by the Meridia stone north of Rihad. They're not allowed inside the walls after dark, poor souls. Funny, isn't it, how the city still sends for them when the dead get up.

notes.title: Night-Oath of the Ash'abah
notes.author: Daria of the Ash'abah
pages:
~We are the ones the cities will not house.
~We wash the dead whom no one else will touch.
~Lady of the shining edge, the bone-singer walks again,
~and he has taken an Ansei from his grave.

The bone-singer Khalil calls himself the Dune-King. He hides in the hollows north-east of this stone, among the dead of Jafar's caravan. He carries the old Ansei's blade, and it sings for him, and that is an insult to every sword-singer who ever lived. We are too few to break him. If a stranger stands here and reads this, Lady, send them to us. The blade must go back into the earth, or into worthy hands.

shrine_molag_bal_hammerfell.hook: A shrine of Molag Bal in the hills north of Taneth, ringed with iron stakes. Slavers who are banned from the Forebear harbour meet their buyers here by night, and pay their tithe to the Lord of Chains.
shrine_molag_bal_hammerfell.rumour: Fisherfolk keep going missing north of Taneth. Everyone knows where they go: the Molag Bal shrine, and a slaver they call Iron-Collar. Lord Ezhar's put a price on him. Nobody's collected.

notes.title: Iron-Collar's Tally
notes.author: Sallah Iron-Collar
pages: Taken from the fishing hamlets, Frostfall: 6. Two strong, three middling, one old woman who will not stop singing. Sold to the Khajiit buyer: 2. Sold to the Bosmer buyer: 1. Tithed to the Lord of Chains: the old woman, at the dark moon, as is proper.

Lord Ezhar has put a price on my head. Very flattering. Taneth sells silk made by children and tigers broken with whips, and calls me the monster. I keep the stock in the pens behind the shrine. Five left. If the Forebears come, kill the stock first. Dead goods tell no tales.

shrine_namira_hammerfell.hook: A shrine of Namira among the dunes south-west of Sentinel, kept by a sect of beggars who live in old tombs and whom the priests of Tu'whacca accuse of robbing the dead of their journey.
shrine_namira_hammerfell.rumour: The Namira folk in the south-west dunes live in the old Yokudan tombs. Priests say they eat what they find in there. I say a priest will say anything to get you to tithe.

notes.title: Testament of a Tomb-Dweller
notes.author: Old Fennah
pages: The priests of Tu'whacca say we rob the dead. The dead do not need robbing. They have nothing and they are going nowhere. It is the living who robbed us: the landlords of Sentinel, the Crowns who took our fathers' fields, the Forebears who took our boats.

So we live where no one will follow. We sleep in the cool stone with the old kings and we are not afraid of them. The Lady of Decay has taught us that everything rots, the rich man's silk and the beggar's rags alike, and that the rot is honest. We do not eat the dead. Mostly. Not unless the winter is very long. Tell the priest that, and watch his face.

shrine_nocturnal_hammerfell.hook: A shrine of Nocturnal in the broken hills south of Elinhir, where the thieves' crews of Craglorn pledge their takings to the Night Mistress. The Observatory's stolen lens is said to lie here now.
shrine_nocturnal_hammerfell.rumour: Craglorn thieves leave a share for Nocturnal at the stone south of Elinhir. Somebody's left a great glass lens there lately. Big as a cartwheel. The mages are beside themselves.

notes.title: Pledge-List of the Dusk Crew
notes.author: Zahra Quickhand
pages:
^For the Mistress, a share of every haul
The purse of a Breton envoy, emptied on the Wayrest road: two pearls to the shrine. A caravan of Skaven silk: one bolt, the grey one, which nobody would buy anyway. The great lens of the Serpent Tower: kept whole, for now.

The mages think the lens is about stars. It is about the Mistress. When the moons are dark and the lens is turned to the sky, it shows the paths of shadow between the stars, and a thief who knows those paths can walk anywhere. We will keep it until the next dark moon. Then the Serpent can find its own way.
