shrine_peryite_hammerfell.hook: A shrine of Peryite in the waste south of Skaven, raised by the survivors of a caravan that was quarantined in the desert during an old fever and left to die by the city it was trying to reach.
shrine_peryite_hammerfell.rumour: The Peryite shrine south of Skaven is where they left the sick caravan in the old plague. Skaven's grandmothers still won't buy goods that came by that road. Some grudges outlive fevers.

notes.title: Journal of the Quarantined
notes.author: Ismail, caravan-master
pages:
#Day 6 outside the walls
Skaven will not open its gates. The fever is in three of the wagons. They throw down bread from the walls and shoot arrows at anyone who comes closer. We have moved to the old stones south of the city, where at least there is shade.

#Day 19
We prayed to the Eight. The Eight did not come. We prayed to the Lord of Pestilence because he, at least, was already here. He came. The fever has stopped spreading. It has not stopped. It only waits, he says, for the order he will give it. He says we are his now, and that one day he will send us back to Skaven. My people are not afraid of that day. They long for it.

shrine_sanguine_hammerfell.hook: A shrine of Sanguine in the vine-covered hills north-east of Rihad, where the young heirs of the Forebear wine houses hold revels so lavish that the losses are settled in vineyards.
shrine_sanguine_hammerfell.rumour: Rihad's young merchant sons go up to the Sanguine stones with a cartload of their fathers' best. They come back with no shoes and a goat. It's always a goat. Nobody knows why.

notes.title: Wager Written on a Wine-Cask Lid
pages:
^Wagered this night of revel, before the Lord of Debauchery and all his cheerful company:
By Tahir son of Barid, vintner's heir of Rihad: twelve casks of his father's gold vintage, against the deed to a vineyard below Kvatch, held by a gentleman in a red mask who says he has never lost a bet in nine hundred years.

Contest: who shall drink the most and still recite the full list of Ra Gada kings.
Result: Tahir, by three cups and one king. The gentleman in red paid his debt with the deed, and a goat, and a curious smile. He said Tahir would understand the goat later. Witnessed by: nobody sober.

shrine_sheogorath_hammerfell.hook: A gaudy shrine of Sheogorath in the hills east of Taneth, kept by a sea captain who sailed off the edge of his own sanity and swears he found a second sea on the other side.
shrine_sheogorath_hammerfell.rumour: Captain Bakr from Taneth gave his ship to the Mad God and walked inland to the shrine. He's been there three years, teaching the lizards to sail. He says they're quick learners.

notes.title: Log of the Landlocked Captain
notes.author: Captain Bakr al-Tanethi, master of the dry dhow 'Pomegranate'
pages:
#Day 1,092 at anchor
Wind: sideways. Sea: sand. Crew: four lizards, a goat and a very patient scorpion. The Lord of the Isles came by at dawn and commended the lizards' knots. I gave him a ration of cheese and a promotion.

#Day 1,093
The Forebear harbour-master sent a letter asking me to return my ship's papers. I have eaten them. They were not seaworthy. The scorpion has mutinied and taken the goat. I will sail after them as soon as the dunes turn to water. The Lord says it will be soon. The Lord says that every morning. Every morning I believe him. That is the only sane thing I have left.

shrine_vaermina_hammerfell.hook: A shrine of Vaermina in the Alik'r dunes south of Sentinel, where nomads once came to buy prophetic dreams and now come in fear, because the dreams have started to come true in the wrong order.
shrine_vaermina_hammerfell.rumour: The Alik'r nomads used to trade at the Vaermina stones for dreams of water. Now they dream of their own deaths, and three of them have already happened. Backwards. Don't ask me how.

notes.title: Warning Knotted in a Camel-Rope
notes.author: Rafiq of the Alik'r
pages: Traveller. My people came to this stone for four generations to buy dreams of where the water lies. The Mistress of Dreams was a fair trader. One dream of water for one of our memories, an old one, of no great use.

This year she is hungry. She takes the new memories now: our children's names, the faces of our wives. And the dreams she gives back are of death, and they come true. My brother dreamed of a scorpion and died of a sting a month before he had the dream. Do not sleep within sight of this stone. If you must sleep, sleep with a pebble under your tongue. It keeps her fingers out.

elden_root.hook: The living capital of Valenwood, built in the boughs of a single colossal graht-oak, where the Silvenar speaks for the Bosmer, the Spinners tell their tales, and Thalmor Justiciars listen to both.
elden_root.rumour: Elden Root's lovely from below and lovelier from above. Just don't say anything about the Thalmor on the high walks. The wind carries. So do the Justiciars.

notes.title: Ordinance of the Thalmor Mission at Elden Root
notes.author: First Emissary Lirinwe, for the Aldmeri Dominion
pages:
^ORDINANCE CONCERNING OBSERVANCES OF A DAEDRIC CHARACTER
The Dominion respects the customs of its Bosmeri subjects, including the Green Pact, which it has never sought to amend. The Dominion does not, however, extend that respect to the worship of Daedric Princes, which is an affront to the Aldmeri inheritance and an ongoing embarrassment.

Accordingly, the shrine north of the city, where certain persons gather to petition the Taskmaster for cures, is placed under observation. Names of petitioners will be recorded. No arrests are contemplated at present. Citizens are reminded that 'at present' is a precise phrase, and that the Dominion uses language precisely.

notes.title: Letter from a Grahtwood Cook
notes.author: Mother Ardrel, of the Bough-Kitchen
pages:
Grandson,
You write from Alinor that the Altmer eat greens and grains and call us savages for eating only meat. Tell them that Y'ffre sang the forest into shape and asked only that we not harm it. Tell them we keep that promise every day, with every meal, and that they cannot say as much for their promises to anyone.

Tell them also, very politely, that the Meat Mandate allows a Bosmer to eat an enemy fallen in battle within three days. Then smile, and show your teeth. That usually ends the dinner. Come home for the Felling Moon festival. I am making jerked boar with redberry wine sauce, and I will not tell you whose recipe it was.

notes.title: A Spinner's Tale, Written Down
notes.author: Told by a Spinner of Elden Root, set down by a Breton listener
pages: Before there were Bosmer there were only the hungry and the hunted, and Y'ffre could not tell which was which. So the Storyteller made a bargain with the Huntsman: the forest would be his hunting ground, and the people his hounds, and in return the hounds would never become the hunted, so long as they kept the Pact.

The Huntsman's stone stands north-west of the great tree to this day. The Bosmer hunters leave the first kill of the year there, and say the old words. The Spinner who told me this tale laughed when I asked whether the Huntsman ever broke his side of the bargain. 'He never has,' she said. 'We have. And then he came hunting.'

falinesti.hook: The walking city of Valenwood, a graht-oak so vast it once strolled from season to season across the forest. Its rootkeepers swear it has begun to stir again, and cartographers weep.
falinesti.rumour: Falinesti's rooted in Malabal Tor this year. Or it was last week. Check before you send a letter. My cousin addressed one there and it came back from Greenshade, slightly chewed.

notes.title: A Cartographer's Complaint
notes.author: Aurelia Venn, of the Imperial Geographical Society
pages:
Dear Society,
I regret to inform you that my survey of Malabal Tor is again incomplete, because the principal landmark has again moved. The Bosmer assure me Falinesti is 'sleeping', and that it only turned over. A city turning over in its sleep is not something one can usefully put on a map.

I have charted what I could. Note in particular the thorn-grove east of the city, where the Bosmer will not go. There is a shrine to Molag Bal at its heart and the trees there grow bent, as though something heavy were pressing down on the canopy. My guide refused to enter. When I asked why, he showed me the chains wound into the roots.

notes.title: Record of the Rootkeepers
notes.author: Rootkeeper Gwaeril
pages:
^Where the Walking Tree has stood, as remembered by the Rootkeepers
Summer of the Red Moon: the banks of the Xylo, where it drank for three years and the river ran low. Winter of the Many Arrows: deep in Malabal Tor, where it hid from the Colovian armies. This year: here, where it has stood longer than any keeper living remembers.

The tree has begun to hum at night, as it did in the old songs before a walk. The young say it is the wind. The old say it is restless because of the felling east of Elden Root. If the Walking Tree walks again, the keepers will go with it, and the Thalmor tax-collectors may chase us through the canopy for as long as they like.

woodhearth.hook: A harbour city of Greenshade grown from a ring of living trees, where Bosmer, Altmer traders and Maormer spies all share the same docks and none of them share the same story.
woodhearth.rumour: Woodhearth's wardens are jumpy. Somebody's been setting fires in the deep forest east of the city. In Valenwood you can kill a man and be forgiven by supper. Burn a tree and you're hunted for life.

notes.title: Notice of the Wardens of Woodhearth
notes.author: Warden Ilthaer, of the Greenshade Watch
pages:
^FIRE IN THE GREEN
Three burns have been found in the forest north-east of the city, each a perfect circle, each at the dark of the moon. At the heart of the newest stands the shrine of the Prince of Ruin, its altar still warm.

Whoever lit these fires has broken the oldest law of Y'ffre and will answer to every hunter in Greenshade. Anyone who knows the names of these firebrands is to come to me at the Warden's bough. Anyone who knows them and stays silent is to consider whether they enjoy being alive.

notes.title: Letter of a Woodhearth Dockhand
notes.author: Thoron the Net-Mender
pages:
Sister,
You asked if it's true about the Mandate-Breakers. It's true. There's a band of them out by the Namira shrine north-east of here. The Green Pact lets us eat what we kill in battle within three days, as you know, and nobody in Woodhearth would turn up their nose at a Maormer leg after a raid.

But these ones don't wait for battles. They don't wait three days. And they've started to say it's not the Pact they serve but the Lady of Decay, who says that all flesh is the same flesh. Two of the net-boys have gone. Their mothers are asking the Wardens. The Wardens are asking whether it's really any of the Wardens' business. That's how bad it's got.

arenthia.hook: A border town of Reaper's March where Bosmer and Khajiit trade, quarrel and drink together beneath stone walls older than either people's memory, and lately where nobody sleeps soundly.
arenthia.rumour: Arenthia used to be a good town for a quiet drink. Now half of it walks the streets at night with its eyes shut. Shazah at the inn says it's the dreams. Shazah's eyes have gone very dark.

notes.title: Letter of Shazah the Innkeeper
notes.author: Shazah, keeper of the Two Moons Inn
pages:
To the Moon-Priest of Rawl'kha,
Shazah writes because no one in Arenthia will listen. Every night this month the sleepers come down out of the houses and walk north, toward the old stones of Vaermina beyond the walls. Bosmer and Khajiit alike, eyes shut, smiling. In the morning they remember nothing but a woman with a purple lantern.

Shazah's own cub walked last night. Shazah followed. There is a Bosmer woman at the shrine who calls herself the Lantern-Bearer, and she sits with a basket and the sleepers drop their dreams into it like fruit. Please send a priest. Or send someone with claws. Shazah does not much care which.

notes.title: Caravan Notice by the Elsweyr Gate
notes.author: Ri'zahd, caravan-master
pages:
^THIS ONE SEEKS GUARDS
Ri'zahd's caravan leaves for Rimmen at the new moon with moon-sugar, silk and many very fine carpets. Ri'zahd pays well. Ri'zahd pays better if no carpets go missing, as they did last time near the shadowed shrine north-west of town.

Ri'zahd knows who took them. Ri'zahd knows the thieves leave a share for the Night Mistress at that stone. Ri'zahd has also left a share at that stone, a larger one, so that the Mistress may think twice before favouring the thieves again. Ri'zahd is not proud. Ri'zahd is practical.

shrine_azura_valenwood.hook: A shrine of Azura in the Grahtwood canopy north-west of Elden Root, built by Khajiit caravans on the long road to Elsweyr, where the Moon-Mother's light falls through the leaves at dusk.
shrine_azura_valenwood.rumour: The cat caravans stop at the Azura shrine on the Grahtwood road and sing to the Moon-Mother. The Bosmer don't mind. They say it's the only time Khajiit are quiet enough to hear a bowstring.

notes.title: Prayer of a Caravan-Mother
notes.author: Ma'jhira, caravan-mother of the Long Road
pages:
~Azurah, Mother of the Twilight, who taught the cats to be cats,
~this one has walked from Rimmen to Elden Root eleven times.
~She asks no more roads. She asks only that the road be kind
~to the young ones who walk it after her.

Ma'jhira's cubs do not know the old prayers. They know the price of moon-sugar in six cities and the names of every Thalmor tax-officer between here and Senchal. They are clever. They are not wise. Teach them, Mother, as you taught Ma'jhira, at the hour when the moons are rising and the sun has not yet gone. That is the only hour when a Khajiit will listen.

shrine_boethiah_valenwood.hook: A shrine of Boethiah deep in Malabal Tor, where Bosmer outlaws who have broken the Green Pact swear themselves to the Prince of Plots, since no tree in Valenwood will shelter them now.
shrine_boethiah_valenwood.rumour: The Kin-Breakers of Malabal Tor took an axe to a living tree and the Green Pact cast them out. Now they pray to Boethiah. Funny thing about outcasts: they always find a god who wants them.

notes.title: Boast Cut into a Felled Log
notes.author: Vanthir the Kin-Breaker
pages: I, Vanthir, cut the living wood. I did it in the open, at noon, before the Silvenar's own messenger, and I did it because the Pact is a leash. The Spinners say Y'ffre made us. Y'ffre made us small and hungry and forbade us to build. Boethiah made nobody, and forbids nothing.

The Prince of Plots asks only that we be strong enough to take what we want and clever enough to keep it. So we have taken this log, and this clearing, and this shrine. Next we will take Falinesti's toll-road. The wardens will come. The wardens always come. And one of them will join us, because one of them always does.

shrine_clavicus_vile_valenwood.hook: A shrine of Clavicus Vile in Greenshade east of Woodhearth, where a famously idle Bosmer once wished never to be hungry again, and has been regretting the precise wording ever since.
shrine_clavicus_vile_valenwood.rumour: Old Faelin out by the Clavicus shrine asked the Prince never to go hungry. Now he's never hungry. Never full, either. Never anything. Eats out of habit. Says meat tastes of rain.

notes.title: Complaint to a Daedric Prince
notes.author: Faelin of Greenshade
pages:
To the Prince of Wishes and his excellent hound,
I wished never to go hungry. I meant: never to want for meat. I meant: never to have to hunt it in the rain. You know what I meant. Your dog laughed when I said it, and I should have known then.

Now I do not go hungry. I do not feel hunger at all. Nor taste, nor satisfaction, nor the warmth of a full belly by a fire. My wife's roast is ashes in my mouth. The Meat Mandate is a mockery to me; I keep it out of duty, like a priest who has lost his faith. I wish to unwish it. Your dog says unwishing costs more. What could cost more than this?

shrine_hermaeus_mora_valenwood.hook: A shrine of Hermaeus Mora in the Reaper's March south of Arenthia, where a Spinner once traded her own memories for every story that was ever told in the forest, and lost her name in the bargain.
shrine_hermaeus_mora_valenwood.rumour: There's a Spinner sits by the Mora shrine south of Arenthia, telling stories nobody else knows. Ask her name and she'll tell you a tale about it. It's never the same name twice.

notes.title: The Unremembered Spinner's Tale
pages:
~I went to the many-eyed one and said: I am a Spinner.
~I carry the tales of my people as the river carries rain.
~But tales are lost when Spinners die, and I am growing old.
~Give me every story, so that none is ever lost.

~He said: there is no room in you for every story
~unless you give me yours.
~So I gave him my mother's face, my wedding, my first kill.
~Now I know the tale of every Bosmer who ever lived,
~and when I come to my own, the page is blank.
^(Carved beneath:) Do not ask her who she is. She will tell you, and she will be wrong.

shrine_hircine_valenwood.hook: An antlered shrine of Hircine in Grahtwood north-west of Elden Root, where Bosmer hunters lay the year's first kill and swear the old oath that keeps the hounds of the Pact from becoming the hunted.
shrine_hircine_valenwood.rumour: Every Bosmer hunter in Grahtwood lays the first kill of the year at the Hircine shrine. The ones who skip it have unlucky seasons. The ones who mock it have short ones.

notes.title: The First-Kill Oath
pages:
~Father of Hunts, we are your hounds.
~We take the deer, and leave the tree.
~We take the boar, and leave the root.
~We take the foe who shoots at us, and leave nothing.

Scratched below in a shaking hand: 'Father, the elders are angry about the felled oak east of the city, and there is talk among them of the old rite, the one that makes the hounds into beasts with no master. Do not answer them. Please. My brother is one of the hunters they would use. I have left you a stag. I will leave you anything else you ask, if you will only stay your hand.'

shrine_malacath_valenwood.hook: A shrine of Malacath in the Grahtwood forest, kept by a clan of Wood Orcs who have lived in Valenwood for centuries, keep a version of the Green Pact all their own, and are tired of being called guests.
shrine_malacath_valenwood.rumour: The Wood Orcs of Grahtwood keep a Malacath shrine in the deep forest. They don't cut trees, they don't build stone, they just glare. Bosmer leave them be. Orc arrows fly as far as anyone's.

notes.title: Words of Chief Murzga Root-Tusk
notes.author: Murzga gro-Dulk, chief of the Root-Tusk clan
pages: Malacath, we came into this forest when the Bretons burned Orsinium the first time. The Bosmer said: you may stay, if you keep our Pact. So we kept it. We cut no tree. We ate only meat. We raised no forge, because a forge needs wood, and we made our blades of bone and stone like our grandfathers' grandfathers.

Five hundred years we have kept their Pact. And still they call us guests. Still the Thalmor tax-men count us twice, once as Orcs and once as trouble. Hear us, Furious One. We do not want their trees. We want our name on the land we have bled for. We want to be from here.

shrine_mehrunes_dagon_valenwood.hook: A shrine of Mehrunes Dagon in the deep Greenshade forest north-east of Woodhearth, ringed by perfect circles of burned trees. In Valenwood there is no worse crime, and someone is committing it on purpose.
shrine_mehrunes_dagon_valenwood.rumour: Someone's burning the forest around the Dagon shrine in Greenshade, a circle at a time. The wardens say it's a cult. The old folk say it's worse: they say it's a Bosmer.

notes.title: Creed of the Ashen Circle
notes.author: Caedwen the Ashen
pages: The Green Pact is a cage of leaves. We are forbidden to build, forbidden to cut, forbidden to change. The Altmer laugh at us, the Imperials log our forests from the east, and still we kneel to trees. The Prince of Ruin teaches that all things must burn to be renewed. The forest will be renewed.

Each circle we burn is a door. When there are nine, the doors will open together and the forest will learn what fire can teach. Six are done. Three remain. I will light the seventh myself, at the shrine, at the dark of the moon. Let the wardens come. Let them see what a Bosmer looks like when she is no longer afraid.

shrine_mephala_valenwood.hook: A shrine of Mephala in the Reaper's March south-west of Arenthia, draped in the webs of great spiders, where a sect of Bosmer weavers gathers secrets for anyone who will pay, including the Thalmor.
shrine_mephala_valenwood.rumour: The web-weavers at the Mephala shrine sell secrets. They sell them to the Khajiit, the Bosmer, the Thalmor. Doesn't matter who's buying. The spiders always get their share.

notes.title: Accounts of the Silken Sisters
notes.author: Sister Ithelia
pages: Sold to the Thalmor envoy at Arenthia: the names of the Khajiit smugglers on the Rimmen road. Price: one hundred gold and the envoy's promise to look away from our grove. Sold to the Khajiit smugglers: the name of the Bosmer who sold them to the Thalmor. Price: two hundred gold.

Sold to the Bosmer elders: the name of the Thalmor envoy's informant in their own council. Price: three hundred gold and the right to weave undisturbed for another year. The Mother of Webs is pleased. Everyone has paid, everyone is betrayed, and no one has thought to ask who sold them out. Feed the spiders. They have earned it.

shrine_meridia_valenwood.hook: A radiant shrine of Meridia in Grahtwood west of Elden Root, where Bosmer hunters of the dead come before they go into the old barrows, since even the Green Pact has no rule against killing what is already dead.
shrine_meridia_valenwood.rumour: Bosmer don't bury their dead deep, so the necromancers love Grahtwood. The hunters who deal with them pray at the Meridia shrine. Then they go into the barrows singing. Gives you chills.

notes.title: Song of the Barrow-Hunters
notes.author: Elthor the Bright-Eyed
pages:
~We are the hunters of the hunters' bones,
~we stalk the stalkers in the burial groves.
~The Pact forbids the axe, the saw, the flame,
~but the Pact has nothing to say of light.

~Lady of the shining edge, we eat no corpse that walks;
~we leave it to your light.
~When the bone-callers come to Grahtwood's dead,
~we will sing as we go in.
~We will sing as we come out.
~And if we do not come out, Lady, sing for us.

shrine_molag_bal_valenwood.hook: A shrine of Molag Bal at the heart of a thorn-grove east of Falinesti, where the trees grow bent and chains are wound into the roots. The Bosmer will not enter. Something inside invites them every night.
shrine_molag_bal_valenwood.rumour: There's a grove east of Falinesti where the trees grow crooked, like slaves under a load. Molag Bal's shrine is in there. The Bosmer won't go near it. They say the trees inside are screaming.

notes.title: Journal of a Captured Warden
notes.author: Warden Aldoril of Falinesti
pages:
#First night
The thing that keeps this grove is a vampire, old, Altmer, who calls the trees her prisoners. She has bound the grove with chains of Coldharbour iron, and each tree she bends is a Bosmer she has drained and planted in the earth. She says the Green Pact forbids me to harm a tree. She says it smiling.

#Fifth night
She has asked me which I would rather be: a tree that cannot move, or a servant that cannot refuse. She says the Lord of Domination gives everyone a choice, and then makes them regret it. I have found a sharp stone. I am going to choose a third thing. If anyone reads this, I chose it.

shrine_namira_valenwood.hook: A shrine of Namira in Greenshade north-east of Woodhearth, held by Mandate-Breakers who claim the Green Pact's oldest law for their own, and who no longer wait for a battle before they feast.
shrine_namira_valenwood.rumour: The Mandate-Breakers out by the Namira shrine say all flesh is one flesh. Two net-boys from the Woodhearth docks are missing. The wardens are still deciding whether it's a Pact matter. I'm not.

notes.title: Sermon of the Mandate-Breakers
notes.author: Gorthil the Lean
pages: Brothers and sisters, the Spinners tell us the Meat Mandate is Y'ffre's gift: eat the foe you slay, so that nothing is wasted. But why wait for a war? Why only the foe? The Lady of Decay teaches that every body is meat in waiting, the elder and the infant, the Altmer and the Bosmer. Waste is the only sin.

We have two of the net-boys from Woodhearth in the pit. They will be our feast at the dark moon. Some among us are squeamish. Some among us say the boys are kin. Kin is a word. Meat is a fact. If the wardens come, we will remind them that the Pact is on our side, and see how long they argue with themselves.

shrine_nocturnal_valenwood.hook: A shadowed shrine of Nocturnal in the Reaper's March north-west of Arenthia, where Khajiit thieves pay their dues to the Night Mistress before working the rich caravans of the Elsweyr road.
shrine_nocturnal_valenwood.rumour: The cat-thieves of the Elsweyr road all pray at the shadow-shrine near Arenthia. Ri'zahd the caravan-master prays there too, and pays more. Says it's cheaper than guards.

notes.title: Vow of the Shadow-Paw
notes.author: Jo'darr Shadow-Paw
pages: Mistress of the Night, this one is Jo'darr. He has taken carpets from Ri'zahd, silk from the Thalmor, and once, a whole roast boar from the Silvenar's own table, with the Silvenar still sitting at it. He leaves you the tusks. They are very fine tusks.

Ri'zahd has also prayed here, Jo'darr knows. Ri'zahd left more gold than Jo'darr. This is cheating, Mistress. A merchant should not bribe the patron of thieves. Jo'darr will steal Ri'zahd's offering and give it back to you twice, so that you are paid by both of us and owe neither. This is fair. This is the way of shadows.

shrine_peryite_valenwood.hook: A shrine of Peryite in Grahtwood north of Elden Root, where sick Bosmer come for cures the Thalmor healers will not give them, and where the Thalmor now quietly write down every name.
shrine_peryite_valenwood.rumour: The Peryite shrine north of Elden Root cures the spore-cough, they say, when the Altmer healers won't. Thalmor have a man with a book in the bushes now. Writing down everyone who goes.

notes.title: A Healer's Recipe, Left at the Shrine
notes.author: Old Maeryn, herb-woman of Grahtwood
pages: For the spore-cough of the deep groves, which the Altmer healers in Elden Root will only treat for those who can pay in Dominion gold: one measure of spriggan sap, one of bear fat, three crushed nirnroot leaves, all burned at the Taskmaster's stone with an honest prayer. Breathe the smoke. Cough the spores. Live.

The Lord of Pestilence keeps order in sickness as in all things. He does not cure for love. He cures because the spore-cough is a disorder and he dislikes disorder. That is enough for me. Note: the Thalmor watcher in the hazel thicket is called Nerion. He has the cough himself. I have left him a pouch of smoke. We will see whose list he writes me on.

shrine_sanguine_valenwood.hook: A shrine of Sanguine in Greenshade south of Falinesti, where Bosmer revellers brew rotmeth strong enough to make a Nord weep and hold feasts that sometimes forget which guests are on the menu.
shrine_sanguine_valenwood.rumour: They brew rotmeth at the Sanguine shrine south of Falinesti. One cup and you sing. Two and you dance. Three and you wake up in Woodhearth married to a Khajiit. I'm told the marriage holds.

notes.title: Rotmeth of the Revel, a Recipe
notes.author: Galthor the Thirsty
pages:
^Sacred to the Lord of Revels
Take the haunch of a boar that died frightened. Seal it in a gourd with its own blood and let it rot for a moon. Add honey, a spoonful of crushed beetle, and three drops of whatever the Khajiit at the next fire is drinking. Bury it under the shrine for nine nights. Dig it up while singing. Do not stop singing.

Warning: drink it only at the stone. Last Midyear, Cousin Faenor carried a gourd home to Falinesti and drank it alone, without singing, and the Lord of Revels was offended. Faenor danced for four days. The rootkeepers had to tie him to a branch. He still taps his foot in his sleep.

shrine_sheogorath_valenwood.hook: A shrine of Sheogorath in the Greenshade forest south-east of Woodhearth, where a Bosmer hunter who once took the Mad God's advice now eats nothing but cheese and claims to be on speaking terms with a tree.
shrine_sheogorath_valenwood.rumour: There's a Bosmer at the Sheogorath shrine south of Woodhearth who gave up meat for cheese. Breaks the Pact, eating cheese. Nobody's sure. The Spinners have been arguing about it for a year.

notes.title: Journal of the Cheese-Eater
notes.author: Halbor, formerly a hunter
pages:
#Day the first of my enlightenment
The Lord of Madness appeared to me as a talking badger and asked why I eat only meat. I said: the Green Pact. He said: and is cheese a plant? I said: no. He said: and is cheese an animal? I said: no. He laughed for an hour and gave me a wheel of Colovian goat cheese.

#Day the three-hundredth
The Spinners cannot decide whether I have broken the Pact. The Silvenar has sent a messenger to ask. The tree beside the shrine has also been asked, and says nothing, which the elders take as disapproval and I take as shyness. I have never been happier. The badger visits on Fredas.

shrine_vaermina_valenwood.hook: A shrine of Vaermina north of Arenthia, where a Bosmer dream-thief called the Lantern-Bearer draws the sleepers of the town out of their beds each night and harvests their dreams in a basket.
shrine_vaermina_valenwood.rumour: The sleepwalkers of Arenthia all go north to the Vaermina stones. There's a woman there with a purple lantern. Shazah at the inn's ready to claw her face off. She'd pay you to do it first.

notes.title: Diary of the Lantern-Bearer
notes.author: Ellidir the Lantern-Bearer
pages:
#Sun's Dusk, the 4th
Bosmer dream of the hunt. Khajiit dream of the moons. Mixed together in my basket they make the most extraordinary colours. The Mistress of the Orb has never tasted their like. She has promised me the purple lantern for good if I fill the basket by the dark of the moon.

#Sun's Dusk, the 11th
The innkeeper's cub had a dream of a great golden cat walking across the sky. It was the loveliest yet. I kept it, and left her only the dark. She will wake screaming every night for a year. The Mistress says that is the tithe. I say it is a small price for something so lovely. The basket is nearly full.

alinor.hook: The white capital of the Summerset Isles and the heart of the Aldmeri Dominion, a city of perfect towers and perfect manners, where the Thalmor govern, the Sapiarchs teach, and everyone is watched.
alinor.rumour: Alinor is the most beautiful city in Tamriel. Everybody says so. Everybody has to. There's a Justiciar on every corner taking notes on who doesn't.

notes.title: Proclamation of the Thalmor Directorate of Alinor
notes.author: The Directorate of Public Virtue
pages:
^CONCERNING THE SHRINES OF THE OUTER HILLS
The Directorate notes with displeasure that the old Daedric shrines in the hills about Alinor continue to receive visitors. These shrines predate the Dominion and are preserved solely as historical curiosities, in the manner of a ruin or a scar.

Citizens of good lineage do not visit scars. Any citizen found at a Daedric shrine after sunset will be presumed to be engaged in research, and will be invited to explain that research to a Justiciar. The invitation may not be declined. The Directorate thanks the citizens of Alinor for their continued and unanimous loyalty.

notes.title: Letter of a Lorekeeper of Alinor
notes.author: Lorekeeper Tirenwe of the Crystal Tower Annex
pages:
Dear Colleague,
You ask why I still keep the memorial roll of the Oblivion Crisis when the Directorate prefers that we celebrate the Dominion's founding instead. Because I was a child in this city when the gates opened. Because I watched the hills north of Alinor burn while the Daedra walked up from the Destroyer's old shrine as if it were a doorway they had always owned.

And because, my friend, someone has begun leaving offerings at that shrine again. Fresh ones. I have reported this to the Justiciars, who thanked me and did nothing, which in my experience means either that they know, or that they do not wish to. I am too old to climb hills. I am looking for someone who is not.

notes.title: Letter of a Quay Porter
notes.author: Ondarion, porter of the Lower Quay
pages:
Brother,
They took Aunt Elerie's daughter away last week. The child was born with a crooked spine and the Directorate's genealogists came to the house with their measuring rods. They were very polite. They always are. They said the family's 'line' would be reviewed. Aunt Elerie said she would rather lose the line than the girl.

So she has lost the line. They are both gone, out to the old Namira shrine west of the city where the cast-outs live, the crooked and the scarred and the ones whose ears are the wrong shape. I took them bread at night. Do not tell Father. He would report me, and then he would weep, and he would do both sincerely.

firsthold.hook: The oldest port of Auridon, a white-walled harbour where every ship from the mainland must anchor under the eyes of the Thalmor before it may continue to the Summerset Isle.
firsthold.rumour: Every ship bound for Alinor stops at Firsthold first. Customs searches your cargo, your crew and your conscience. Somebody called the Moth has been searching their strongboxes in return.

notes.title: Report of the Firsthold Customs House
notes.author: Inspector Valanir, Auridon Customs
pages:
#11th of Frostfall, 4E 201
The Breton carrack 'Fair Winifred' has been refused entry and towed to the quarantine anchorage. Three of her crew present the grey blisters. In accordance with the Directorate's orders, the crew may not land. In accordance with nature, they are dying.

It is reported that some of the anchorage's sick are rowing ashore by night to the Peryite shrine north-west of the town, to beg the Taskmaster for what our healers will not give. I have not ordered them stopped. I would like this report to record that I have not ordered them stopped. I would like it to record also that I have a family, and that they live in Firsthold.

notes.title: Informant's Note to the Justiciars
notes.author: A loyal citizen (name on file)
pages:
Esteemed Justiciars,
The thief who calls herself the Moth has robbed the house of Magistrate Caladwe again. Jewels, a ledger, and the Magistrate's ceremonial circlet. I have seen her at the Nocturnal shrine west of the town at dusk, a slight figure, an Altmer by her height, and dressed like a scholar.

I believe she hides her takings near the shrine, for she goes there laden and comes back light. I ask in return only that my son's application to the Sapiarchs be looked upon kindly. I am told that loyalty is its own reward. I am also told that it is not the only one.

artaeum.hook: The misty isle of the Psijic Order, which appears off the Summerset coast only when the monks of the Old Ways wish to be found. Sailors who have seen it rarely agree on what they saw.
artaeum.rumour: My father saw Artaeum once, through the fog off Alinor: a white tower and an old man waving. Next morning, nothing but sea. He never fished that water again. Said it felt like he'd been interrupted.

notes.title: A Fisherman's Account
notes.author: Naril, fisherman of Alinor
pages: I write this down because no one in the tavern believes me. On the night of the 3rd of Hearthfire I was out past the western shoals in the fog, and the fog opened like a door. There was an island, green and gentle, with orchards and a white tower, and bells ringing so softly I felt them more than heard them.

A woman in a grey robe stood on the shore and looked straight at me. She did not wave. She simply nodded, as if I had arrived exactly when expected, and then the fog closed and I was alone with my nets. My nets were full. They had been empty before. I have never caught fish like those before or since. They tasted of time.

notes.title: Words on a Stone by the Shore
pages:
^Cut into a white stone on the shore, in a hand that is very old and very patient
The Old Ways are not a door. They are the wall in which the door is set.
What the Altmer call purity, we call stillness. What the Thalmor call order, we call a cage that has not yet noticed it is a cage.

Time is a river that remembers its banks. Do not try to swim against it. Do not try to drink all of it. Sit on the bank, and wait, and you will see everything you have lost come floating by.
If you are reading this, you were invited. Do not be proud of it. So was the fish.

shrine_azura_summerset.hook: A shrine of Azura in the hills north of Alinor, where Altmer of old families still come at dusk to honour the Queen of Twilight, and Thalmor Justiciars come to write down their names.
shrine_azura_summerset.rumour: The Azura shrine north of Alinor's the only Daedric stone the old families still visit openly. Twilight's beautiful, they say, and beauty's not illegal. Not yet.

notes.title: Surveillance Report, Azura Shrine
notes.author: Justiciar Aranelya, Directorate of Public Virtue
pages:
#Observation of the 7th to the 14th of Hearthfire
Visitors at dusk: eleven. Of these, six of established lineage (names attached), three of uncertain lineage, one Bosmer servant, one elderly scholar who claimed to be 'sketching the light'. The scholar's sketches have been confiscated. They are, regrettably, very good.

Assessment: the cult of the Twilight Queen among the Altmer is aesthetic rather than devotional. The visitors are moved by the hour and the colour of the sky rather than by the Prince. Recommendation: continued observation, no action. Personal note, to be removed before filing: I have been watching this shrine for two years. The light at dusk here is the loveliest I have ever seen. I do not know what to do with that.

shrine_boethiah_summerset.hook: A shrine of Boethiah on Auridon south-west of Firsthold, where young Thalmor officers are rumoured to make secret offerings for advancement, and senior officers are rumoured to have made them first.
shrine_boethiah_summerset.rumour: The ambitious ones in the Thalmor pray at the Boethiah stone on Auridon. Not officially, of course. Officially there's no ambition in the Thalmor. Only loyalty, and sudden vacancies.

notes.title: Diary of a Junior Agent
notes.author: Agent Telonir, Auridon Station
pages:
#Rain's Hand, 4E 201
The Station Chief has held his post for forty years. He will hold it forty more unless something changes. I have served loyally. I have filed every report. Loyalty is apparently a ladder with no rungs. Tonight I went to the old shrine on the hill and asked the Prince of Plots for a rung.

#Second Seed
The Station Chief's deputy has been recalled to Alinor, under a cloud. I did not cause it. I merely noticed something and mentioned it to someone. The deputy's post is vacant. I have been asked to fill it, temporarily.
#Midyear
The Station Chief has begun to look at me oddly. I have begun to look at him the same way. It is very instructive, this shrine.

shrine_clavicus_vile_summerset.hook: A shrine of Clavicus Vile in the hills south of Alinor, where an Altmer lord of falling fortunes once traded for an heir of perfect blood. He got one. He has never been able to look at her.
shrine_clavicus_vile_summerset.rumour: Lord Ondeneth asked the Clavicus stone for a child with perfect lineage. The Directorate's genealogists couldn't fault her. That's what bothers him. Nobody's that perfect. Not even the Thalmor.

notes.title: A Lord's Confession
notes.author: Lord Ondeneth of the House of the Seven Spires
pages:
To the Prince of Bargains,
My house was failing. Our lineage was questioned; a Bosmer great-grandmother, they said, of whom no record should have survived. My wife was barren. I came to this shrine and asked for an heir whose blood the Directorate could not fault. You gave me Laerwen.

She is perfect. Her lineage is perfect. Her ears, her eyes, her manners, her magic, all perfect. She does not cry. She has never cried, not even as an infant. My wife died the night she was born and Laerwen did not look up. Your dog told me that what I paid with was 'the family resemblance.' I understand now. She is not like us. She is like what we pretend to be.

shrine_hermaeus_mora_summerset.hook: A shrine of Hermaeus Mora on Auridon north-west of Firsthold, where a circle of Sapiarch students reads from a folio that the Crystal Tower struck from its catalogue three hundred years ago.
shrine_hermaeus_mora_summerset.rumour: The young Sapiarchs sneak off to the Mora shrine on Auridon to read some forbidden folio. Two of them came back speaking backwards. The Tower says it is the strain of their examinations.

notes.title: Notes of a Sapiarch Student
notes.author: Eradil, candidate of the Crystal Tower
pages: The Unnumbered Folio was removed from the Tower's catalogue in the Third Era by order of the Sapiarchs, who called it 'an inquiry the Altmer are not yet ready to complete'. We found it here, in the shrine, in a box of black wood that opens only when you are not looking at it. Every night we read one page. Every night the page is different.

Last night's page explained, quite clearly, how the Aldmeri lineage might be traced back beyond the Dawn Era, to whatever the Aldmer were before they were Aldmer. Caelinor laughed and laughed and then could not stop. The keeper of the folio, a robed thing with too many eyes in its hood, says the answer is on the next page. We are all going back tonight.

shrine_hircine_summerset.hook: A shrine of Hircine in the wild south-west of the Summerset Isle, where Altmer lords once hunted for sport, and where something from the last hunt has never stopped hunting them back.
shrine_hircine_summerset.rumour: The Altmer lords stopped holding hunts at the Hircine shrine after the Faralan boy came back on four legs. They say he's still out there in the scrub. The lords say it's a fox. A very large fox.

notes.title: Report of the Royal Game-Warden
notes.author: Warden Sorondil, of the Alinor Preserves
pages:
To the Directorate,
As instructed, the annual Lords' Hunt has been suspended. I record the reason plainly, since no one else will. During the hunt of 4E 199, the young lord Faralan of the House of the Seven Spires separated from the party near the old shrine of the Huntsman. He was found at dawn, bitten, and laughing.

He was confined to the family's estate. He is no longer confined anywhere. The deer in the south-west preserve have become very few, and the shepherds of the hill farms very nervous. I request permission to hunt the creature. I am told that it is a member of a noble house and may not be hunted. I am told to call it a fox.

shrine_malacath_summerset.hook: A shrine of Malacath on Auridon south of Firsthold, kept by Orc dockhands who work the Firsthold quays and who remind every Altmer who sneers at it that the Orcs were once Altmer too.
shrine_malacath_summerset.rumour: The Orc dockers of Firsthold pray at the Malacath stone south of town. Altmer priests call it Trinimac's grave. The Orcs say if it's a grave, it's a grave with a very long memory.

notes.title: Prayer of the Firsthold Dockers
notes.author: Grashak gro-Durz, foreman of the Third Quay
pages:
~Malacath, you who were Trinimac,
~the high elves made you a god and then made you a monster,
~and they think that settles it.
~They do not know that we remember.

Lord of the Spurned, the Altmer of Firsthold pay us half what they pay their own and call it generosity. They let us carry their crates but not walk their streets after dark. Give us patience, so that we do not drop their crates on their feet. Give us strength, so that we do not need to. And give the overseer Varanil a long and itching rash. You know where.

shrine_mehrunes_dagon_summerset.hook: A shrine of Mehrunes Dagon in the hills north of Alinor, where the Daedra came through during the Oblivion Crisis. A memorial to the dead stands beside it, and someone has begun leaving fresh offerings again.
shrine_mehrunes_dagon_summerset.rumour: Someone's leaving blood at the Dagon shrine north of Alinor, right next to the memorial to the Oblivion dead. The Justiciars say it's vandals. Old Tirenwe at the Tower says vandals don't chant.

notes.title: Memorial to the Fallen of the Crisis
pages:
^In memory of the citizens of Alinor who fell in the hills above the city
^when the gates of the Deadlands opened, 3E 433
Here the Daedra came. Here the city's guard and its mages, its scholars and its fishermen held them until the gates closed. Here we buried them. Their names are written on the Tower's roll, and on the hearts of those who are left.
Below, scratched in recent days, in a neat hand: 'The gates did not close. They were only waiting. The Lord of Destruction remembers Alinor fondly, and will return to it by the same road. -- V.'

notes.title: Ledger of the Returning Dawn
notes.author: Vorondil, Keeper of the Returning Dawn
pages: The Thalmor promised the Altmer a return to glory. They give us genealogy tables and curfews. The Prince of Destruction promised the world an ending, and he keeps his promises. The Mythic Dawn failed because it was clumsy. We will not be clumsy.

Offerings made: twelve. Dremora summoned and bound: two, both of the Valkynaz. The third will come at the dark of the moon, and with three, the old gate in the hillside can be reopened for the space of a breath. A breath is enough. Alinor never thanked its dead. Let it join them.

shrine_mephala_summerset.hook: A shrine of Mephala on Auridon south of Firsthold, where those who inform for the Thalmor, and those who inform on the informers, leave messages for one another in the webs.
shrine_mephala_summerset.rumour: Want to know who's informing for the Justiciars in Firsthold? Ask at the Mephala stone. Want to know who's informing on the informers? Same stone. Same spiders, too.

notes.title: A Letter Left in the Web
notes.author: Signed only with a spider drawn in ink
pages:
To the one who reads this next,
The Justiciars of Auridon pay twelve gold for every name of a disloyal citizen. They pay twenty for the name of a disloyal Justiciar. They pay nothing at all for the name of the person who has been selling them both lists for nine years. That is because they do not know that person exists.

I serve the Mother of Whispers, and I serve the Thalmor, and I find the two services almost identical. Both demand that you trust no one, that you remember everything, and that you smile. The only difference is that the Mother of Whispers admits it. If you would like to know your own name on the lists, leave fifty gold in the web. I will not tell you which list.

shrine_meridia_summerset.hook: A shining shrine of Meridia in the hills west of Alinor, where an old Altmer lamp-keeper has tended the light every night for two centuries, and has never once let a walking dead thing past it.
shrine_meridia_summerset.rumour: The lamp-keeper at the Meridia shrine west of Alinor is older than the Dominion. The Justiciars tried to move her on once. They came back down the hill rather quickly and very sunburned.

notes.title: Lamp-Keeper's Log
notes.author: Ellaraine, keeper of the bright stone
pages:
#The 30,112th night
Lamp lit at sunset. Oil: good. Wick: trimmed. Necromancers in the hills: one, a student of the Tower who had read too much and been loved too little. Raised a cat. Cat put down by the light. Student sent home with a stern word and a biscuit.

#The 30,113th night
Lamp lit. Justiciars came, two, to ask under whose authority I keep a Daedric shrine. I told them: under the authority of everyone who has not been eaten by their grandmother. They wrote it down. I hope they file it. The Lady of Light enjoys a jest. She enjoys it more when the jest is true.

shrine_molag_bal_summerset.hook: A shrine of Molag Bal on Auridon west of Firsthold, where a renegade Justiciar is said to have carried out interrogations that even the Thalmor would not sanction. The shrine has not been the same since.
shrine_molag_bal_summerset.rumour: There's a Justiciar who got thrown out of the Thalmor for being too cruel. Think about that. He's at the Molag Bal shrine west of Firsthold now, asking questions. Nobody sends him the questions.

notes.title: Interrogation Notes, Unsanctioned
notes.author: Former Justiciar Haldaril
pages: Subject: Bosmer, male, accused of sedition. Question: who wrote the pamphlet? Answer, after the first hour: he did. Answer, after the second hour: his brother did. Answer, after the third: the Silvenar himself. All three answers are false. Truth is not the purpose. The purpose is the moment he stops caring which answer I want.

The Directorate dismissed me for excess. The Directorate does not understand its own work. The Lord of Domination does. Every interrogation is a small prayer to him: the slow bending of a will until it no longer remembers being straight. He is pleased. He has shown me the Coldharbour in every cell. I will build one here.

shrine_namira_summerset.hook: A shrine of Namira in the hills west of Alinor, the refuge of Altmer cast out for being born imperfect. The Directorate pretends it does not exist. Its people pretend they do not mind.
shrine_namira_summerset.rumour: The crooked ones live out by the Namira shrine west of Alinor. Born wrong, the genealogists said. They're the kindest folk on the island, my mother says. She's not supposed to know that.

notes.title: Verses of the Imperfect
notes.author: Elerie of the Hill
pages:
~They measured my daughter with rods of silver,
~her spine, her ears, the gap between her eyes.
~They found her wanting, and they wrote it in a book,
~and the book was closed, and she was gone.

~Lady of all ugly things, of the beetle and the scar,
~you do not measure. You do not count.
~You take what the beautiful ones throw away,
~and you call it yours, and it is.
~Here on the hill my daughter laughs. Her spine is crooked.
~Her laugh is perfect. Write that in your book.

shrine_nocturnal_summerset.hook: A shrine of Nocturnal on Auridon just west of Firsthold, where the thief called the Moth makes her offerings, and where, the Justiciars believe, she hides what she takes from the island's most loyal houses.
shrine_nocturnal_summerset.rumour: The Moth's robbed Magistrate Caladwe four times. Took his ceremonial circlet last month. The Justiciars say she stashes her takings by the Nocturnal stone. They've dug up half the hill and found nothing.

notes.title: A Letter Signed with a Moth
notes.author: The Moth
pages:
To whoever is clever enough to find this, and not a Justiciar,
I am leaving the island before the Directorate's hounds catch my scent. My takings stay behind. I have no use for Caladwe's circlet; I only took it because he wore it while he signed the order that sent my brother to the quarantine anchorage.

Everything I took from him is buried thirty paces north of the shrine, beneath the twisted cypress with the moth carved on its root. Take it. Sell it. Give some to the sick in the anchorage, if you have a heart. The Night Mistress keeps nothing, and neither should you.

shrine_peryite_summerset.hook: A shrine of Peryite on Auridon north-west of Firsthold, where the sick of the quarantine anchorage row ashore by night to pray, because the Directorate's healers will not treat anyone not on the census.
shrine_peryite_summerset.rumour: The sailors from the quarantine anchorage row to the Peryite shrine at night. Customs knows. Customs looks the other way. Customs, I think, has a heart. It won't last.

notes.title: A Sailor's Plea
notes.author: Jory Penwick, bosun of the 'Fair Winifred'
pages: Lord of Sickness, I am a Breton and a sailor and I never prayed to any god but Kynareth and the price of pepper. My captain is dead of the grey blisters. Half my crew is dead. The Altmer will not let us land and will not let us leave. We are anchored off Firsthold like a fish nobody will gut.

You keep order in plague, they say. Then keep it now. Let it take me if it must, but let it pass over the boy Tam, who is twelve and stowed away and should never have come. In return I will do whatever a bosun can do for a Prince. I can tie very good knots. I can curse in nine languages. I am leaving my mother's ring on the stone. It is all I have.

shrine_sanguine_summerset.hook: A shrine of Sanguine just south-west of Alinor's walls, where the city's most decorous lords shed their decorum once a season in revels the Directorate officially knows nothing about.
shrine_sanguine_summerset.rumour: The Sanguine revels south of Alinor are the worst-kept secret in the Dominion. Half the Directorate goes. The other half takes notes. They swap places every season.

notes.title: Invitation, Embossed in Gold
pages:
^The Lord of Revels requests the honour of your indiscretion
^at his stone beyond the south-west gate
^upon the night of the Directorate's Founding Feast
Dress: none required. Masks: obligatory. Lineage: irrelevant, for one night only. Conversation on the subjects of genealogy, the Thalmor and the correct shape of ears is forbidden on pain of a forfeit.

Note, in a cramped hand on the back: 'Darling, last year you wore the Justiciar's sash and nobody knew it was you. Wear it again. It caused the most delicious panic. And do bring the Bosmer wine, the illegal one. The Prince adores contraband. So do I. -- L.'

shrine_sheogorath_summerset.hook: A shrine of Sheogorath in the hills south-west of Alinor, decorated by an Altmer painter who was expelled from the Academy for painting the sky the wrong colour, and who has been painting it every colour since.
shrine_sheogorath_summerset.rumour: The mad painter by the Sheogorath stone paints the sky green, the sea purple, and the Justiciars as chickens. They keep confiscating the chickens. He keeps painting more.

notes.title: Manifesto of the Painter of Wrong Colours
notes.author: Aicantar the Unhung
pages: The Academy of Alinor teaches that there are seven acceptable blues for the sky over Summerset, and that a painter who uses an eighth is not merely wrong but disloyal. I used an eighth. I was expelled. The Lord of Madness visited me that very night and said the sky had complained to him that it was tired of being blue.

So I paint it green on Morndas and red on Tirdas and on Sundas I let it choose. I paint the Justiciars as chickens because they asked me to paint them as they truly are. I paint the Directorate as an empty frame. Nobody has confiscated that one. Nobody has understood it.

shrine_vaermina_summerset.hook: A shrine of Vaermina in the hills north-west of Alinor, where a Sapiarch of dreams conducts studies of the sleeping mind that the Crystal Tower funds, and is careful never to ask about.
shrine_vaermina_summerset.rumour: There's a Sapiarch who studies dreams at the Vaermina shrine. Pays volunteers a gold piece a night to sleep there. Nobody volunteers twice. Some of them haven't woken up from the first time.

notes.title: Observations on the Sleeping Mind, Draft
notes.author: Sapiarch Ilaeril of the Faculty of Dreams
pages: Subject the Fourth (Bosmer servant, paid one gold): dreamed of the forest. On waking, could not remember the word for 'tree'. Subject the Ninth (Altmer clerk, paid one gold): dreamed of his own funeral, in great detail, attended by no one. On waking, resigned from the Directorate and went to sea.

Hypothesis: the Mistress of the Orb does not create nightmares. She reveals the nightmare that already lies beneath each sleeper. Altmer nightmares are uniformly about being found imperfect. I find this academically significant. I find it personally disquieting. Subject the Twelfth will be myself.
